# SOURCE_FILE: DPFs/Engineering DPF Suite/README.md
---
# Engineering DPF Suite

**Design, realize, change and sustain functioning systems.** Use this Suite when you need an engineered result whose design, provision, integration and conditions of use must agree. It covers physical and software systems as well as the access and semantic arrangements on which work depends.

A task can finish with a sufficient analysis, design, recommendation or justified decision to keep the current arrangement. An actual system change requires evidence of that change; approving a model or specification does not establish it.

Links to fpf.tools open readable text; **Markdown** links and the CAD entries below open the repository source. GitHub previews can truncate large files. Check the [displayed source edition](https://fpf.tools/status) when the version matters.

## How this Suite is organized and why

**[Read the Engineering Architectural Reference](ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md).** It explains how systems engineering, maintenance, knowledge access, semantic integration and control architecture design fit together, why organizational and human specializations have their own Suites, and how these contributions meet in a working system. Read it for the overall design and its alternatives; use a familiar sufficient method directly when that is all your task needs.

## Keep the project reasoning together

The **[system-thinking long mantra (FPF A.1.STM)](https://fpf.tools/A.1.STM)** connects the intended use and common target to functioning, construction, ways of obtaining the system, capable creators and their cooperation. Its questions hold large areas of knowledge together: a good component, capable team and approved plan still have to fit the same project.

Use the [connected explanation in Engineering.Reference:0.5](ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#engineeringreference05---the-system-thinking-long-mantra-across-engineering-contributions) to see how the Suite's contributions constrain one another. The mantra's order helps explain and remember the reasoning; actual work can begin at any consequential question and return as answers change. The full Methods supply the knowledge needed to answer those questions.

## Reduce avoidable work and repeated firefighting

A faster operation can still produce an unneeded result, repeat an error or leave the result waiting elsewhere. Use **FPF C.42, Reduce Avoidable Work While Preserving the Needed Result**, to construct a worthwhile change, compare its complete burden and make it usable in later work. Its elegance mantra connects these questions without imposing one work sequence. The **[engineering application](ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#engineeringreference06---the-elegance-mantra-and-reducing-repeated-firefighting)** explains how systems engineering, operations and method introduction contribute.

## Choose an entry


| Your question | Open |
| --- | --- |
| How do we design a new system and choose its architecture? | [Develop linked use and system concepts (SYSE.2)](https://fpf.tools/SYSE.2), [construct functional and implementation alternatives (SYSE.5)](https://fpf.tools/SYSE.5), and [decide the architecture and when to reopen it (SYSE.6)](https://fpf.tools/SYSE.6). |
| Which observations, memory, commands and execution conditions can make a control design feasible? | [Choose observations and internal state (CAD.5)](CONTROL-ARCHITECTURE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cad5---choose-observations-and-internal-state-for-control); use the [planning-and-feedback branch (CAD.1–CAD.4)](CONTROL-ARCHITECTURE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cadreference4---the-layered-planning-and-feedback-branch) when that separation is useful. |
| Should we build, buy, commission, reuse or combine ways to obtain a result? | [Compare ways to obtain the result (SYSE.24)](https://fpf.tools/SYSE.24), including integration, capability, support and eventual replacement. |
| How do we keep a system fit for use or restore it after a failure? | [Maintenance Engineering and Management](https://fpf.tools/MNT). |
| How do we make a changing body of knowledge usable in real work? | [Knowledge-Corpus Access Engineering](https://fpf.tools/KCAE). |
| How can systems exchange usable meaning when their sources disagree or change? | [Semantic Integration Engineering](https://fpf.tools/SIE). |
| Which contributions are missing between a local action and the intended whole? | [Method-vertical examples (Engineering.Reference:25.1)](ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#engineeringreference251---what-must-be-available-through-the-method-vertical): a worked explanation with links to the full methods. |
| How do we change an AI agent's execution procedure and test it in work? | [Construct and revise the procedure (SYSE.47)](https://fpf.tools/SYSE.47), then use [representative work to test the agent and its support (SYSE.46)](https://fpf.tools/SYSE.46) when that evidence is needed. |

The [Engineering Architectural Reference](ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md) helps when the question spans several contributions. It explains their connections and leads to full methods; a known sufficient pattern can be used directly.

**Patterns** counts full pattern bodies. **Text, M characters** measures each complete Markdown framework, including its embedded Architectural Reference, in millions of Unicode characters with spaces and original line breaks, rounded to three decimals. These are scope indicators, not a required reading load.

These five frameworks are the current direct coverage, not a claim to cover all engineering branches. Platform Engineering is developed within Systems Engineering. The organizational specialization has its own [Management Suite](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/); the human specialization has its own [Human Capability Engineering Suite](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/).

## Connect the contributions

Consider a laboratory introducing an automated measurement service. Systems Engineering connects the instrument, software, operator and receiving experiment. If controlled motion or temperature is needed, Control Architecture Design connects observations, permitted commands and execution limits for that loop. Semantic Integration makes sample identities, units and reported results agree across interfaces. Knowledge-Corpus Access makes the applicable procedures and evidence retrievable. Maintenance establishes how the measurement capability will remain available.

The project may also need Organization Change Engineering to establish who accepts a sample or releases a result, and Human Capability Development to develop the operator's missing ability. Those methods come from their specialized Suites. Somatic Movement Modeling matters only if bodily coordination limits the work. This is one possible combination, not a required sequence or a requirement to use every contribution.

The dependencies can change a design in either direction: maintainability can change architecture, attainable operator performance can change automation, and a semantic mismatch can require a different interface. Use the [architecture account (Engineering.Reference:0)](ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#engineeringreference0---engineering-specialization-and-maintenance) when the field boundaries or these specializations matter.

## Use engineering in continuing development

Engineering changes and sustains systems. Open-ended development grows knowledge and available ways of acting, puts them to use and continues to further attainable problems. A new instrument or production capability can enable that continuation; completing its installation alone does not establish it.

Use [FPF Core](https://fpf.tools/FPF) for the general methods of development and methodological work. Use domain contributions for the actual realization. Financial, research and strategic results can constrain an engineering choice without becoming an engineering design. Find those suppliers in the [DPF catalogue](../).

For music and dance, engineered performing configurations and environments are part of a wider field that also includes creation, performance and cultural continuation. [Music and Dance Practice Engineering](https://fpf.tools/MDPE) and [Embodied Rhythmics](https://fpf.tools/RHY) retain their own frameworks. The [Reference's capability and performing-practice account (Engineering.Reference:0.4)](ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#engineeringreference04---capability-development-and-wider-performing-practices) explains where their contributions meet engineering.

## Reading, use and reuse

Read [Using FPF Library](../../USING-FPF.md) before applying the methods, with or without an AI assistant. Start from the contribution your work needs; the order of files is not a project sequence. Read a selected pattern's conditions, explanation and worked cases. A checklist helps inspect a result; it does not replace the method.

Anatoly Levenchuk, with AI-assisted development and review. These publications continue to evolve; check the edition when relying on a particular result. # SOURCE_FILE: DPFs/Foundational Thinking DPF Suite/README.md
---
# Foundational Thinking DPF Suite

**Construct, justify and revise models, mathematical and physical accounts, algorithms and notation.** Use this Suite when familiar formulas or operations do not yet connect into the answer you need, or a changed question makes an earlier construction inadequate.

A theorem, physical explanation, algorithm, interpreted model or usable notation can itself be the result. These methods also help develop new ways of working. They do not cover all intellectual activity, all mathematics and physics, or the whole of computer science.

Framework and method links open readable text on fpf.tools; **Markdown** links open the repository source. GitHub previews can truncate large files. Check the [displayed source edition](https://fpf.tools/status) when the version matters.

## How this Suite is organized and why

**[Read the Foundational Thinking Architectural Reference](FOUNDATIONAL-THINKING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md).** It explains why mathematics, physics, modeling, algorithms and notation have distinct frameworks, how their results constrain one another, and how they contribute to inquiry and further development. Read it for the overall design and its alternatives; use a familiar sufficient method directly when that is all your task needs.

## Choose an entry


The following entries contain worked connections, not just pointers to smaller operations. Start from the contribution whose inputs are available; an example's presentation order is not a prescribed project sequence.

| What you need to do | Follow the worked connection |
| --- | --- |
| Combine separately calculated results—for example, obtain an overall mean from departments of different sizes | [Change a combining rule (MATH — MP-COMBINE-RESULTS)](https://fpf.tools/MATH/mathematical-thinking---readme/practical-entries/mp-combine-results---change-a-rule-so-that-separately-obtained-results-can-be-combined): expose the lost distinction, construct a summary and operation, prove their compatibility, then use and revise them. |
| Decide a question without reconstructing every hidden detail | [Obtain a sufficient answer (MMP — MMP-SUFFICIENT-ANSWER)](https://fpf.tools/MMP/mathematical-modeling---readme/practical-entries/mmp-sufficient-answer---answer-the-working-question-before-reconstructing-every-detail): expose what reduction loses, bound its effect, interpret the result and obtain more where it changes the answer. |
| Decide whether another observation will improve an action | [Connect intervention, information and choice (MMP — MMP-INTERVENTION-AND-INFORMATION)](https://fpf.tools/MMP/mathematical-modeling---readme/practical-entries/mmp-intervention-and-information---decide-whether-an-observation-will-improve-the-next-action): derive the relevant consequences, compare the report's benefit with its burden, and make the subsequent choice depend only on timely information. |
| Replace expensive component models and still obtain a usable joint answer | [Replace and couple models (MMP — MMP-REPLACE-AND-COUPLE)](https://fpf.tools/MMP/mathematical-modeling---readme/practical-entries/mmp-replace-and-couple---use-cheaper-models-without-losing-the-combined-answer): retain the required responses, connect their meanings and error bounds, and refine only what prevents the answer. |
| Develop a physical prediction and decide which observation matters | [Connect physical accounts and observations (PHY — PH-PREDICT-AND-DISTINGUISH)](https://fpf.tools/PHY/physical-thinking---readme/practical-entries/ph-predict-and-distinguish---develop-a-physical-prediction-and-the-test-it-needs): constrain the law, derive a consequence, compare the observations that matter and revise the affected premise. |
| Construct an algorithm and adapt it when the required answer changes | [Keep construction and output consistent (CMP — CP-ANSWER-UNDER-LIMITS)](https://fpf.tools/CMP/computational-thinking---readme/practical-entries/cp-answer-under-limits---obtain-the-answer-the-work-needs-within-available-resources): construct the recurrence, share results, use bounds where they reduce search, and revisit what may be discarded. |
| Change a requirement consistently in a formula, an operation diagram and a table | [Keep meaning and change connected (NOT — NT-CHANGE-TOGETHER)](https://fpf.tools/NOT/notational-engineering---readme/practical-entries/nt-change-together---carry-a-changed-request-through-several-representations): recover references and interpretation, expose translation losses, and update the affected expressions. |
| Connect mathematics to changes in working methods | [Understand and change a construction (Foundational.Reference:3.2)](FOUNDATIONAL-THINKING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#foundationalreference32---understand-and-change-a-construction): retain the distinction a later operation uses and connect it to the general Methods of methodological development in Core. |
| Make reasoning available to other contributors and develop its next use | [Continue and distribute thinking (Foundational.Reference:3.5)](FOUNDATIONAL-THINKING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#foundationalreference35---continue-and-distribute-thinking): recover a missing relation, arrange explanation or support, change the work and preserve the method for further development. |

The [Foundational Thinking Architectural Reference](FOUNDATIONAL-THINKING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md) helps choose and combine contributions when no single entry suffices. Its [vertical of ongoing work (Foundational.Reference:3.9)](FOUNDATIONAL-THINKING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#foundationalreference39---keep-the-vertical-visible-while-doing-the-work) helps locate missing intermediate methods, abilities or resources between a local action and its larger purpose.

## Frameworks in this Suite

| Framework | What you can work on | Patterns | Text, M characters |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| [Mathematical Thinking (MATH)](https://fpf.tools/MATH) · [Markdown](MATHEMATICAL-PRACTICE-DPF.md) | Construct mathematical objects, operations and alternatives; derive consequences and meet proof obligations. | 20 | 0.480 |
| [Mathematical Modeling (MMP)](https://fpf.tools/MMP) · [Markdown](MATHEMATICAL-MODELING-PRACTICE-DPF.md) | Relate a subject question to mathematics; infer, predict, compare interventions, design observations and revise or combine models. | 17 | 0.574 |
| [Physical Thinking (PHY)](https://fpf.tools/PHY) · [Markdown](PHYSICAL-THINKING-DPF.md) | Construct and test physical accounts; select interactions and idealizations, derive consequences and distinguish them by observation. | 10 | 0.305 |
| [Computational Thinking (CMP)](https://fpf.tools/CMP) · [Markdown](COMPUTATIONAL-THINKING-DPF.md) | Construct algorithms that obtain the required answer within correctness, resource and interaction conditions. | 16 | 0.438 |
| [Notational Engineering (NOT)](https://fpf.tools/NOT) · [Markdown](NOTATIONAL-ENGINEERING-DPF.md) | Design expressions, interpretations and transformations that make operations usable and changes recoverable. | 8 | 0.221 |

**Patterns** counts full pattern bodies. **Text, M characters** measures each complete Markdown framework, including its embedded Architectural Reference, in millions of Unicode characters with spaces and original line breaks, rounded to three decimals. These are scope indicators, not a required reading load.

## Connect the contributions

Predicting an oscillating system can require a physical account, a model with stated idealizations, a mathematical consequence, an algorithm for the approximation and notation whose variables and units remain interpretable. A measurement that defeats the idealization returns to the physical and modeling premises; computing more accurately cannot repair that defect. Conversely, a numerical error need not invalidate the physical law.

These are different grounds for a connected result: mathematical validity, physical adequacy, computational feasibility and intelligibility of expression. Each matters only where that claim is made. A pure proof needs no invented physical test, and a notation problem need not start with a physical question. For example, `q + q = 2*q` remains an identity, while `read() + read()` need not equal `2*read()` when each call obtains a new value.

The Reference explains [how the contributions constrain one another (Foundational.Reference:2.2)](FOUNDATIONAL-THINKING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#foundationalreference22---relations-that-form-the-field) and [what preserves or changes the field (Foundational.Reference:2.3)](FOUNDATIONAL-THINKING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#foundationalreference23---the-whole-its-continuity-and-its-boundaries). The connected methods remain independently usable.

## Develop and use new ways of thinking

A useful construction can make a new question approachable; an unexplained observation, counterexample or successful new tool can reveal the next question. This Suite supplies the subject-specific constructions. [FPF Core](https://fpf.tools/FPF) supplies general methods for inquiry, methodological development and continuing development. Merely finishing a calculation does not establish that wider continuation.

Research Method Practice, Decision Design, Explanation Design and Narrativization retain their own subjects in the [DPF catalogue](../). They are not absorbed into this Suite because they involve thinking. [Engineering](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/) supplies realization of instruments and other systems; [Human Capability Engineering](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/) supplies changes in people's capabilities. Obtaining an intellectual result, constructing its means and learning to obtain it are different contributions.

## Reading, use and reuse

Read [Using FPF Library](../../USING-FPF.md) before applying the methods, with or without an AI assistant. Start from the contribution your work needs; the order of files is not a project sequence. Read a selected pattern's conditions, explanation and worked cases. A checklist helps inspect a result; it does not replace the method.

# SOURCE_FILE: DPFs/Human Capability Engineering DPF Suite/README.md

# Human Capability Engineering DPF Suite

**Help a person become able to do something, recover an ability or keep it usable.** This Suite connects knowledge of how people change with methods for changing their capabilities and testing them in the work that needs them.

The person is the holder whose capability changes. A teacher, AI assistant or provider organization may perform part of the work. This edition covers learning and somatic contributions through two full frameworks; it does not offer comprehensive methods for the whole organism, personality, health or personal management.

Framework and method links open readable text on fpf.tools; **Markdown** links open the repository source. GitHub previews can truncate large files. Check the [displayed source edition](https://fpf.tools/status) when the version matters.

## How this Suite is organized and why

**[Read the Human Capability Engineering Architectural Reference](HUMAN-CAPABILITY-ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md).** It explains why learning and somatic change are connected here, what makes this an engineering specialization, and which needs require other fields. The two available frameworks do not cover every kind of human change. Read it for the overall design and its alternatives; use a familiar sufficient method directly when that is all your task needs.

## Choose an entry


| Your question | Open |
| --- | --- |
| Does a person's difficulty actually require a capability change? | [Diagnose whether capability, misconception or behaviour limits work (HCD.3)](https://fpf.tools/HCD.3). The needed result may instead be a tool, condition, explanation or specialist contribution. |
| How do explanation, varied experience and participation combine in learning? | [Connected learning cases (HCD.Application:10)](https://fpf.tools/HCD.Application:10), covering language, partnered movement, a clerk's work and an engineering team. |
| Why does a familiar movement fail when bodily experience and voluntary regulation do not connect to the action? | [Model the bodily contribution to a movement (SOM.1)](https://fpf.tools/SOM.1). Suitable technique and physical conditions remain necessary. |

Read the full conditions and cases, including the competence needed to provide the teaching. A course, completed exercise or another performer's output alone does not show the person's capability in later work.

## Frameworks in this Suite

| Framework | What you can work on | Patterns | Text, M characters |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| [Human Capability Development (HCD)](https://fpf.tools/HCD) · [Markdown](HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) | Connect later work to capability demand, personal programmes, learning products, individual and shared practice, feedback, assessment, transfer and retention. | 29 | 1.138 |
| [Somatic Movement Modeling (SOM)](https://fpf.tools/SOM) · [Markdown](SOMATIC-MOVEMENT-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) | Connect bodily experience, regulated effort and coordinated movement; adapt within a familiar movement practice as support or load changes. | 5 | 0.069 |

**Patterns** counts full pattern bodies. **Text, M characters** measures each complete Markdown framework, including its embedded Architectural Reference, in millions of Unicode characters with spaces and original line breaks, rounded to three decimals. These are scope indicators, not a required reading load.

## Connect the contributions

A learner may understand a movement and succeed in a local exercise yet still fail the intended whole action. HCD connects the capability target, practice, feedback and transfer; SOM supplies particular methods for bodily distinctions and regulation when those are the missing contribution. SOM specializes part of that human subject, rather than forming a second obligatory stage for every learner.

The [Human Capability Engineering Architectural Reference](HUMAN-CAPABILITY-ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md) explains the assembly, alternatives and limits. Its [movement example (HCE.Reference:3)](HUMAN-CAPABILITY-ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#hcereference3---how-do-the-contributions-meet-in-a-whole-action) follows the contributions into a whole action; its [outside contributions (HCE.Reference:6)](HUMAN-CAPABILITY-ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#hcereference6---which-needed-contributions-remain-outside-this-edition) show what this edition does not supply.

## Capability and continuing development

Successful work with external help may meet the immediate need without the person learning the helper's method. Learning a known method can also be a complete bounded result. Continuing development asks a further question: what new attainable problems and ways of further development does the acquired capability make available?

Use [Core's connected development method (C.40.OD)](https://fpf.tools/C.40.OD) for that wider undertaking and this Suite for its human mechanisms. The Reference distinguishes [the different results (HCE.Reference:1)](HUMAN-CAPABILITY-ENGINEERING-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#hcereference1---what-is-being-changed-and-for-which-result).

This is the human specialization of [Engineering](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/). Use [Management](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/) when the required change concerns an organization's capability, commitments, authority or resources. Arranging shared learning remains within HCD when the intended result is each person's learning: [compare individual and group arrangements (HCD.20)](https://fpf.tools/HCD.20) and [form learning work groups (HCD.21)](https://fpf.tools/HCD.21).

Developing an AI or robot requires its own mechanisms; a common capability question does not justify transferring human learning or somatic methods unchanged. For an agent's execution procedure and its testing, the [Engineering entries](../Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/#choose-an-entry) lead to SYSE.47 and SYSE.46. Other technical changes require the methods for the actual system; this is not a promise of complete robot-learning or AI-training coverage.

## Reading, use and reuse

Read [Using FPF Library](../../USING-FPF.md) before applying the methods, with or without an AI assistant. Start from the contribution your work needs; the order of files is not a project sequence. Read a selected pattern's conditions, explanation and worked cases. A checklist helps inspect a result; it does not replace the method.

# SOURCE_FILE: DPFs/Management DPF Suite/README.md
---
# Management DPF Suite

**Connect direction, commitments, resources and collective work.** Use this Suite when a promising direction, an accepted promise and the available means do not yet fit together, or a changed condition calls for a different commitment.

The undertaking can be a company, public service, temporary collaboration or voluntary community. A shared employer is unnecessary, but contributions, resources and authority need an actual basis. A smaller promise, sufficient existing arrangement or justified refusal can be the useful result.

Framework and method links open readable text on fpf.tools; **Markdown** links open the repository source. GitHub previews can truncate large files. Check the [displayed source edition](https://fpf.tools/status) when the version matters.

## How this Suite is organized and why

**[Read the Management Architectural Reference](MANAGEMENT-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md).** It explains why strategy, commitments, operations, resources, communities and organizational change belong in one connected management account, what each contributes, and which related disciplines remain outside this Suite. Read it for the overall design and its alternatives; use a familiar sufficient method directly when that is all your task needs.

## Choose an entry


| Your question | Open |
| --- | --- |
| Which direction and investment are worth pursuing? | [Strategy](https://fpf.tools/STR). |
| How can production or service be arranged, and current work meet its promises? | [Operations Management](https://fpf.tools/OPS); use [Organization Administration](https://fpf.tools/ADM) for permissions, provision and obligations. |
| How do we answer different clients without losing repeatability or scale? | [Manage client variation and develop repeatable offerings (CUST.1)](https://fpf.tools/CUST.1). Its constituent methods also work for a bounded offering, delivery or transition question. |
| How do we direct personal action, establish joint direction and sustain participation? | [Leadership](https://fpf.tools/LDR) and [Community Management](https://fpf.tools/CB), according to the missing result. |
| Do roles, authority or capability allocations need to change? | [Organization Change Engineering](https://fpf.tools/OCE). |

For a connected case, the [Management Architectural Reference](MANAGEMENT-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md) follows both a [voluntary practice network (Management.Reference:5.1)](MANAGEMENT-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#managementreference51---a-voluntary-practice-development-network) and [a new order in an operating business (Management.Reference:5.2)](MANAGEMENT-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#managementreference52---a-new-order-in-an-operating-business).

## Keep strategic decisions connected

The **[strategizing mantra (STR.18)](https://fpf.tools/STR.18)** connects **strategic question → worthwhile contribution → explained way → feasible contributions and means → justified choice and commitment → realization, use and renewed questions**. An attractive direction can lack an obtaining way; individually affordable initiatives can compete for the same people; a useful preparation can finish without authorizing implementation. The developed account explains how to assemble and revise these answers, including when a technological possibility comes first or an existing answer is enough.

## Keep operating decisions connected

The **[operational mantra (OPS.23)](https://fpf.tools/OPS.23)** connects local work to the result the operation must deliver: **accepted result → route and readiness → limiting conditions → release and feasible order → service, money and human conditions → observed result and changed conditions**. Its developed account explains the grounds, branches and returns. Increasing a team's activity can leave delivery unchanged; a changed resource window can require revising both starts and promises. Read this account when those decisions need to be made together, rather than treating the phrase order as a work schedule.

| [Organization Administration (ADM)](https://fpf.tools/ADM) · [Markdown](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) | Make requests, permissions, obligations, provision, records and provider coordination effective without unnecessary burden. | 15 | 0.302 |

**Patterns** counts full pattern bodies. **Text, M characters** measures each complete Markdown framework, including its embedded Architectural Reference, in millions of Unicode characters with spaces and original line breaks, rounded to three decimals. These are scope indicators, not a required reading load.

## Connect the contributions

An attractive new order can require a revised offering, delivery capacity, a financial commitment and a change in who may authorize work. Each can look feasible alone while the combination exceeds shared capacity. The Suite helps connect those judgements and revise the offer, provision or commitments together. Use only the contributions needed by the undertaking; Corporate Governance and Corporate Finance retain their corporate conditions.

Management can change an organization's functioning while retaining its organization chart. OCE develops deliberate organizational construction, but does not exhaust management. The [Architectural Reference](MANAGEMENT-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md) explains this organizational specialization of engineering and its [coverage limits (Management.Reference:7)](MANAGEMENT-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#managementreference7---continuity-and-coverage).

For maintained equipment, [Maintenance Engineering and Management](https://fpf.tools/MNT) supplies its full methods from Engineering. For a person's capability, use [Human Capability Engineering](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/). A manager may perform a method when capable or obtain its result from another contributor. The [organizational construction and maintenance account (Management.Reference:3.1)](MANAGEMENT-DPF-SUITE-REFERENCE.md#managementreference31---organizational-construction-and-maintenance-use) explains how organizational choices and maintenance conditions constrain one another.

## Organize conditions for continuing development

A development undertaking may need strategy, participation, time, funding and authority as well as learning or research. This Suite helps arrange those conditions. It does not equate everyday operations, implementing a known practice or one organizational change with open-ended development.

Use [Core's connected development method (C.40.OD)](https://fpf.tools/C.40.OD) when acquired capability should open further attainable problems and the means to continue. An office, distributed responsibility at workplaces, an external provider and AI-assisted arrangements are alternatives to examine from the required methods and conditions, not names that settle the design.

## Reading, use and reuse

Read [Using FPF Library](../../USING-FPF.md) before applying the methods, with or without an AI assistant. Start from the contribution your work needs; the order of files is not a project sequence. Read a selected pattern's conditions, explanation and worked cases. A checklist helps inspect a result; it does not replace the method.

Anatoly Levenchuk, with AI-assisted development and review. These publications continue to evolve; check the edition when relying on a particular result. For a method, cite its framework, edition and complete PatternID.

# Domain Principle Frameworks

**Find a field's methods for the result you need.** These 34 frameworks explain domain practice through connected patterns, with conditions, worked cases and source grounds. Use them for a current task or as contributions to continuing development; applying a method once does not require a development programme.

If you know the field, choose a Suite or framework below. If you only know the difficulty, describe it in ordinary words and search the texts; [Using FPF Library](../USING-FPF.md#choose-what-to-read) explains how to find and connect useful contributions. The [Library introduction](../) gives the overall purpose and a first-use route.

Framework and method links open readable text on fpf.tools; **Markdown** links open the repository source. GitHub previews can truncate large files. Check the [displayed source edition](https://fpf.tools/status) when the version matters.

## How the frameworks fit together

**[Read the Library Architectural Reference](../FPF-LIBRARY-REFERENCE.md)** to understand why these disciplines are grouped into Suites, why other frameworks stand alone, and how to use contributions across their boundaries. Each Suite’s introduction also opens its own Architectural Reference: the explanation of that Suite’s composition, choices and limits. The tables below help you select publications; those accounts explain the arrangement.

## Suites


A Suite brings together constituent disciplines and explains how their knowledge and practices work together. Open its folder for a task-oriented introduction, the framework files and its Architectural Reference.

| Suite | Working subject | DPFs | Patterns | Text, M characters |

| [Management](Management%20DPF%20Suite/) | Direction, commitments, operations, resources, markets, communities and organizational change. | 12 | 187 | 5.216 |

| [Human Capability Engineering](Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/) | Human learning and somatic change, connected to capability in later work. | 2 | 34 | 1.207 |

## Further domain frameworks

These ten fields have their own files here. They are not a fifth Suite: research, decisions, narratives and the other subjects do not become one discipline merely because their files share a folder.

These are scope indicators, not a required reading load. Suite totals sum their constituent frameworks and exclude the separate Suite Reference.

## Combine only the contributions your work needs

For example, a decision may require a research finding, a mathematical model and an explanation to its participants. Decision Design, Research Method Practice, Foundational Thinking and Explanation Design then supply different results. Read the relevant conditions and connect those results; you do not need to study every framework or use every pattern in sequence.

When the purpose is to expand an agent's capabilities and continue to further attainable problems, use [Core's connected development method (C.40.OD)](https://fpf.tools/C.40.OD) with the relevant domain methods. The particular changes needed by a person, AI, team or organization differ.

Every full framework has one home in the Library. Using its methods elsewhere does not add a second membership. An embedded Framework Architectural Reference explains its pattern language; Suite References explain the larger disciplinary assemblies. The [Library Architectural Reference](../FPF-LIBRARY-REFERENCE.md) explains the boundaries and connections across them.

## Reading and reuse

Before applying the methods, follow [Using FPF Library](../USING-FPF.md). A folder alone does not contain external frameworks its methods may need. [FPF Core](https://fpf.tools/FPF) supplies the common concepts and transdisciplinary methods.

Anatoly Levenchuk, with AI-assisted development and review. Publications evolve with their methods and uses. Original content is available under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); see [licensing terms](../LICENSING.md). Cite the framework, edition and full PatternID for a specific method.


# SOURCE_FILE: Readme.md

# FPF Library

**Methods for solving difficult problems, expanding what you can do, and continuing development.**

FPF Library brings together the **First Principles Framework (FPF Core)** and domain frameworks for people, AI agents, teams and organizations. It offers ways to reason, investigate, design, coordinate work, learn and improve the methods used to do those things. Each method is explained as a pattern: a recognizable difficulty, the conditions in which it arises, a way to obtain a useful result, worked cases and limits.

The Library is developing as a **methodology of open-ended development**. A result can make a previously unattainable problem approachable; working on that problem can expand both your capabilities and your ways of developing them. The aim is to keep that continuation possible, without a predetermined final level. This includes noticing limitations that have not yet become explicit problems, using existing knowledge, constructing missing methods, and passing useful capabilities and knowledge to others.

You can also use one method for one calculation, design, decision or learning need and stop there. A completed task, a new procedure or learning a known method does not by itself establish continuing development.

[Start using the Library](USING-FPF.md) · [Domain frameworks](DPFs/) · [FPF Core](https://fpf.tools/FPF)

## How the Library is organized and why

**[Read the Library Architectural Reference](FPF-LIBRARY-REFERENCE.md).** It explains why general methods belong to Core, why some disciplines form Suites while others have standalone frameworks, and how their contributions work together. Use it to get an overview, understand an apparent overlap or judge a proposed change.

For a familiar task, you can go straight to a suitable method below.

## Start with your work

You do not need to read the Library from beginning to end. Bring a situation, the result you need and what currently prevents you from obtaining it. Choose an entry below, or search the publications for the difficulty in ordinary and technical language.

| What you are trying to do | Where to begin |
| --- | --- |
| Find a way to obtain a result when the familiar answer is insufficient | [Find and develop a way to obtain a result (FPF C.39)](https://fpf.tools/C.39). It connects existing answers, missing constructions and the use that needs the result. |
| Develop your own, a team's or an organization's ability to continue beyond its present limits | [Construct and continue open-ended development (FPF C.40.OD)](https://fpf.tools/C.40.OD), together with the domain methods needed for the actual change. |
| Design, acquire, integrate or maintain a functioning system | [Engineering](DPFs/Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/). |
| Make direction, promises, resources and collective work fit together | [Management](DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/). |
| Obtain or check a mathematical or physical answer, model, algorithm or notation | [Foundational Thinking](DPFs/Foundational%20Thinking%20DPF%20Suite/). Apply the needed method yourself or have a capable specialist or AI apply it; learning to perform it yourself is a separate choice. |
| Help a person acquire or retain a capability for later work | [Human Capability Engineering](DPFs/Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/). |
| Investigate a question, design a decision, explain material or work in another field | [Further domain frameworks](DPFs/#further-domain-frameworks), including research, decision design, explanation and narrativization. |

Before applying a method, read [Using FPF Library](USING-FPF.md). It explains how to find a useful contribution, read its conditions, connect it to the rest of the work and distinguish a source citation from a direction to apply another method. An adequate known answer can be used directly; a larger question may need several connected methods. Their order in a file is not an instruction to perform them all.

## Keep connected reasoning in view

**Long mantras** help recall how answers to related questions depend on one another. For a project, the **[system-thinking long mantra (FPF A.1.STM)](https://fpf.tools/A.1.STM)** connects intended use, a common target, functioning, construction, ways of obtaining it, capable creators and their cooperation. Its full explanation shows why those answers must fit and what to revisit when one changes.

The **[control mantra (FPF C.43)](https://fpf.tools/C.43)** connects assessment of the situation, possible continuations, comparison and choice, realization, examination of what happened and revision. Its full Method explains how observations can change later choices, how means and timing constrain them, and how an intervention can develop the capability to address further problems. Technical control, economic choices and developmental recommendation retain their particular mechanisms.

A mantra is a logical teaching unfolding, not a fixed order of thinking or work. The [Library's account of connected reasoning (Library.Reference:1.1)](FPF-LIBRARY-REFERENCE.md#libraryreference11---long-mantras-and-connected-reasoning) leads to developed connections in several fields. Read the full account to understand and adapt the method; use the short formula to recall it.

## From a useful result to further development

Suppose a team can deliver its current product, but a more demanding order is beyond its capabilities. Buying a specialist's result might meet the immediate need. Learning to produce it would change what the team can do. Learning how to recognize the next limitation, obtain or invent a needed method and organize its acquisition would change how the team can continue developing. These are different results, with different evidence.

The Library helps connect them without requiring the same arrangement everywhere. A person working with an AI, several collaborating teams and a company with a development office need different domain methods and allocations of work, resources and authority. An office is one possible arrangement, not a prerequisite for development.

The general methods are in **Core**: [connect development work (C.40.OD)](https://fpf.tools/C.40.OD), [connect a method, the capability to perform it and the conditions for its use (C.40.JD)](https://fpf.tools/C.40.JD), and [continue from a result to new attainable problems (C.40.NP)](https://fpf.tools/C.40.NP). The DPFs supply the particular mechanisms of learning, research, engineering, management and other practices. Developing a method, changing an agent's capability and actually performing work remain distinct contributions.

## What is available

**FPF Core** contains 400 patterns in 17.697 million characters. It supplies transdisciplinary concepts and methods, including methodological work and open-ended development. **34 Domain Principle Frameworks (DPFs)** supply subject-specific methods: 24 belong to four Suites, and ten have their own files directly in the DPF catalogue.

A DPF describes one field through a connected pattern language. A **Suite** describes a composite discipline through its constituent fields and their relations. An **Architectural Reference** explains how the relevant language is arranged and why: within a framework, across a Suite, or across the Library.

| DPF Suite | Working subject | DPFs | Patterns | Text, M characters |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [Engineering](DPFs/Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/) | Designing, realizing, changing and maintaining systems; knowledge access, semantic integration and control architecture design. | 5 | 99 | 2.791 |
| [Management](DPFs/Management%20DPF%20Suite/) | Direction, commitments, operations, resources, markets, communities and organizational change. | 12 | 187 | 5.216 |
| [Foundational Thinking](DPFs/Foundational%20Thinking%20DPF%20Suite/) | Mathematical and physical accounts, models, algorithms and usable notation. | 5 | 71 | 2.017 |
| [Human Capability Engineering](DPFs/Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/) | Human learning and somatic change, connected to capability in later work. | 2 | 34 | 1.207 |

The [DPF catalogue](DPFs/) lists the ten further frameworks and opens each Suite's files. Suite totals sum their constituent framework texts; separate Suite References and README pages are excluded. Character counts include spaces and original line breaks. Counts describe the available material, not how much you must read before using it.

The Library does not claim to exhaust the disciplines it covers: the current Human Capability Engineering Suite, for example, develops learning and somatic contributions, not all methods concerning a human being.

## Read online or use your own copies

Read [Core on fpf.tools](https://fpf.tools/FPF), or choose a [domain publication](https://fpf.tools/publications) and open the required pattern. The first method links above open that reading service. GitHub cannot display the complete Core and may truncate large DPFs; a link to a valid heading does not remove that limit.

For the source, open the [Core Markdown file and its history](FPF-Spec.md) or [download Core as raw Markdown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ailev/FPF/main/FPF-Spec.md). Framework tables on these pages provide Markdown source links and, where available, online reading links. On fpf.tools, **Copy and source** identifies the repository edition behind the displayed passage. Check [source editions and update status](https://fpf.tools/status) when the version matters; the service may lag behind GitHub. [Search](https://fpf.tools/search) and [MCP connection instructions](https://fpf.tools/connect) provide other ways to reach the material.

For local use, download or clone this repository. Keep `FPF-Spec.md`, `FPF-LIBRARY-REFERENCE.md`, `USING-FPF.md`, the licensing files and `DPFs/` in their existing arrangement. A selected subset is also usable: include the actual supplying frameworks needed by your question, not just links to unavailable files. [Using FPF Library](USING-FPF.md#make-the-publications-available) explains access and selection.

### Work with an AI assistant

Give the assistant access to the full relevant texts, your actual situation, constraints and observations. Put this instruction in the project settings or instruction file the agent actually reads, replacing `fpf/` with your location:

> Use FPF Library from `fpf/`. Before applying its methods, read `fpf/USING-FPF.md` and follow its guidance. Help obtain the result our work needs. Explain the reasoning in our working language, identify the patterns used, and distinguish source claims, assumptions and missing evidence.

Then ask a concrete question. For example: “Our team can deliver the current product but not the proposed variant. Help compare acquiring an external result, developing our capability and changing the offering. What information could change that choice?”

An assistant can retrieve methods, calculate, compare alternatives, draft and challenge reasoning. Its fluent answer does not establish an observed fact, a new capability, permission, a commitment or an implemented system. Check the output against the actual work, evidence and applicable decision authority. FPF Library is a method library, not an agent runtime or a grant of autonomous authority. It is intended for human use as well as AI-assisted work, across physical, organizational, intellectual and embodied practices.

## Understand, check or extend a contribution

README pages help you choose; full patterns teach the methods and state their conditions. Read the exact explanation when a recommendation matters. A maintained account of useful approaches can include competing schools, failures and limits; neither the newest standard nor one successful example establishes universal applicability.

For a precise reference, retain the complete PatternID or section address and enough context to identify the publication. [Using FPF Library: resolve a portable reference](USING-FPF.md#resolve-a-portable-reference) explains how this works across files, search and MCP. You need not learn document codes before choosing what to read.

For an [issue or proposed improvement](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/issues), identify the publication and passage, the working situation, what failed or remains unavailable, and the change you propose. Use the relevant Architectural Reference to understand the current design. The broader FPF ecosystem can include independently authored DPFs, local frameworks (LPFs), guides, tools and services; this repository publishes FPF Library.

## Author, status and reuse

**Anatoly Levenchuk, with AI-agent assistance.** The publications are usable and continuously revised: an “eternal alpha.” That describes continued development, not a guarantee of suitability for every use. Cite the publication, edition and pattern when their identity matters.

Original framework content is licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). See [licensing terms](LICENSING.md) for attribution, third-party material and software boundaries. Sharing or adapting licensed text requires the applicable attribution and change notices. Independently authored DPFs and LPFs may use their authors' chosen licenses; using the methods or publication form does not by itself impose CC BY.

### Citation

```text
Levenchuk, Anatoly. FPF Library.
GitHub repository: https://github.com/ailev/FPF
```

For a specific claim or method, add the publication, edition and complete PatternID.

# Readme

## Start with the missing result

Two people can use the same word for different problems; two models can answer different questions despite displaying the same measure. PSDA.1 and PSDA.2 make the formulation and boundary examinable. PSDA.3 constructs complementary model claims. A clear question with adequate models needs none of that work again: it can enter directly at an alternative, value, uncertainty or comparison result.

When a promising change leaves other participants' work unexplained, use [PSDA.20](#psda20---explore-a-situation-through-goals-and-dependencies). Start from the actual episode and trace one needed provision through its recipient, purpose and provider. The inquiry can return an omitted condition or a new question before a comparison is ready; its car-park case follows the return from a favorable model result to conflicting assignments.

When familiar proposals cannot obtain a desired consequence, start with [PSDA.5](#psda5---generate-decision-alternatives). Its constructive return through PSDA.6 and PSDA.8 helps build a different combination of means and test it under the same conditions.

If the proposed intervention is already familiar but its value is disputed, PSDA.6 separates attributed concerns, protected conditions and compensating trade-offs. PSDA.8 compares consequences only under a declared rule. PSDA.9 tests where the conclusion holds or reverses. A retained set or bounded conditional comparison can be the complete answer; the authorized chooser makes the later choice.

If a discussion contains reports and opinions but no usable conclusion, B.5.SD constructs the missing inference with competent contributors. Professional facilitation can supply the participation conditions through PSDA.13. It may also supply the subject integration when the facilitator has that competence. A clear direct explanation needs no meeting.

An assisting agent can explain or apply these Methods in ordinary language. Ask for the actual objects, differences, grounds and next useful action, rather than a list of framework names.

## A comparison can be correct and still answer too little

Consider a constructed inquiry about a pumping arrangement. One formulation concerns rated capacity; another concerns access to assistance when roads fail. The second changes the boundary and model question. A capacity model does not establish that people can reach help or that a mobile pump can be deployed. PSDA.1–3 preserve those differences before a comparison is used.

For an illustrative analytical slice, fixed pumps have losses 2 with normal roads and 3 with road access lost, at cost 8. Mobile pumps have corresponding losses 1 and 9, at cost 5. With assumed road-loss probability `p` and cost weight `λ`, lower-is-better scores are `2 + p + 8λ` and `1 + 8p + 5λ`. Fixed pumps score lower when `7p > 1 + 3λ`. At `λ = 0.5`, the mobile score is lower for `p = 0.2`, but the fixed score is lower for `p = 0.6`.

PSDA.6 keeps the assumed trade-off distinct from protected service conditions. PSDA.7 keeps the missing probability basis visible. PSDA.8 supplies the conditional comparison and PSDA.9 exposes its reversal. Neither assumed input is established by this arithmetic. The incumbent and a staged direction may also remain live outside this two-option slice. A whole-investment recommendation therefore requires additional qualified premises or a narrower return.

Now suppose deployment is unavailable in the required window. The mobile branch loses its applicability; inserting a convenient probability cannot repair it. The fixed-option arithmetic remains valid at its stated scope. A professional adviser uses PSDA.14 to return what the recipient can rely on, while the governing decision remains separate. An analyst studying the relation for understanding can instead stop with the bounded model result.

## Practical entries

Bring the question that is blocking useful work. The examples below show how professional support uses intellectual inquiry and returns a qualified answer, and how a changed premise can send that use back. They are not a catalogue or a required sequence. Use the pattern index or search when another question is live; an adequate direct result can finish the task. The [Architectural Reference](#decision-design-principles-framework-architectural-reference) and its [Architectural Rationale](#psdareference5---why-retain-this-connected-language) explain how the contributions fit together. You can ask an assisting agent: “Explain this and give me your comments in ordinary language, without framework jargon.”

If the useful future contribution itself is still unclear, use the general [C.40.OCN opportunity construction (FPF C.40.OCN:1)](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#c40ocn1---problem-frame) directly. You can construct an opportunity and stop at its next question without appointing an adviser. When a distinct performer must recommend a development direction to a recipient, use the [advising profile](#development-direction-advising) or the second example below.

### PSDA-CARD-01 — Turn a contested situation into a usable recommendation

- **Situation:** A municipal committee needs advice on a pre-season pumping arrangement. Operations staff emphasize capacity, residents raise unequal protection, and responders question safe access and deployment.
- **Question:** What can the inquiry recommend while preserving those differences and the committee's investment authority?
- **First useful result or blocker:** Attributed formulations and a usable inquiry boundary; then a conditional comparison whose omissions remain visible in the recommendation.
- **Start with:** [PSDA.11](#psda11---bound-the-decision-support-engagement-and-authority-boundary) for the receiving question and authority boundary. If these are adequate, enter at the missing participation, formulation, model or comparison result.
- **Stop or return:** Return the supported advice or its limitation through `PSDA.14`. Reopen the dependent model, alternative, scope or recommendation when a material concern or premise changes. The committee retains the later choice.

The constructed [flood-pump application](#psdaapplication1---app-psd-01--a-flood-pump-calculation-is-not-the-whole-investment-answer) begins with an independent inquiry team preparing a return for the committee. `PSDA.12` discovers affected people and concerns beyond those able to attend. `PSDA.1` preserves different formulations: insufficient capacity, unequal protection, fragile maintenance and unsafe deployment. Their consequences inform the `PSDA.2` boundary: compare the pre-season pumping arrangements while keeping material downstream effects and mobility constraints visible. Long-term relocation remains outside this inquiry.

That boundary changes the modeling question. `PSDA.3` keeps nominal pumping capacity separate from whether people can reach assistance and whether a mobile pump can arrive when roads fail. `PSDA.4` compares a capacity-only calculation with a bounded combination of attributed inquiry and conditional technical analysis. The combination is useful only if its contributions can be obtained and their subjects, conditions and meanings can be joined. `PSDA.13` lets participants correct the claim “the pumps protect the district”: a capacity result does not answer the separate access question. A concern map supplies questions for comparison, not numerical weights.

`PSDA.5` retains the current arrangement, fixed pumps, mobile pumps and a still-incomplete staged direction. The following slice compares only fixed and mobile pumps. Its loss and cost figures are illustrative units, not measured impacts or a complete investment account.

| Alternative | Loss with normal roads | Loss with road access lost | Cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fixed pumps | 2 | 3 | 8 |
| Mobile pumps | 1 | 9 | 5 |

With an assumed road-loss probability `p` and cost weight `λ`, the illustrative lower-is-better scores are `2 + p + 8λ` and `1 + 8p + 5λ`. `PSDA.6` keeps the trade-off premise separate from protected conditions; its §4.5 constructs compatible preferences when the exchange still needs elicitation, with a deterministic worked case in §5.5. `PSDA.7` retains the missing basis for `p` and the uncertainty conditions needed here. `PSDA.8` supplies the comparison, and `PSDA.9` exposes its reversal: fixed pumps score lower when `7p > 1 + 3λ`. At `λ = 0.5`, mobile pumps score lower for `p = 0.2`, but fixed pumps do for `p = 0.6`. Neither input is established for the committee's decision by this calculation.

The `PSDA.14` return therefore retains the conditional comparison while withholding a whole-investment ranking. Access, assistance and protection conditions remain unqualified; the baseline and staged direction were not disposed of by the two-row calculation. A further result is requested through `A.15.9` only if its obtainable contribution warrants the burden. Even resolving road access would not by itself settle the value trade-off.

Suppose the committee authorizes a study, and a qualified source then establishes that mobile deployment is unavailable during the required window. `PSDA.15` returns to the mobile alternative and its consequence premises; this is not a reason to insert a convenient value of `p`. Preserve the earlier conditional calculation as such, but do not use it as the current investment basis. If a newly affected group reveals an omitted consequence, return to the boundary as well. Study authorization still leaves pump procurement to its own decision.

### PSDA-CARD-02 — Recommend a development direction without taking the choice

- **Situation:** A separate advisory team must recommend a ninety-day reliability direction for a service organization: internal development, an external provider or a mixed human–AI arrangement.
- **Question:** Which direction or information-gaining step do the available premises support, and which claims remain conditional?
- **First useful result or blocker:** A retained set with its comparison limit, or a supported direction or bounded probe recommendation when the missing premises become available.
- **Start with:** `PSDA.11` for the engagement; then use `PSDA.5`, `PSDA.6`, `PSDA.7`, `PSDA.8`, `PSDA.9`, `PSDA.14` at the first missing result. The [profile](#development-direction-advising) and [development-direction application](#psdaapplication2---app-psd-02--development-direction-advice-with-unlike-holder-premises) supply the connected account and its other holder cases.
- **Stop or return:** Give the supported advice with its material limits. Use `PSDA.15` for a real changed-premise or follow-up question, preserving independent claims. The authorized chooser decides whether to commit or probe.

In the constructed organization case, the committee has the stated mandate, and the advisory service's competence, confidentiality and conflict conditions are met. Reliability takes priority over throughput; security, critical-service continuity and a bounded probe budget are protected. The operating account identifies the recovery contribution, an interface account describes the current arrangement, and a priority statement supplies the receiving value. These inputs help define the `PSDA.5` alternatives, but none compares all three whole arrangements.

The first `PSDA.14` return retains internal development, the provider and the mixed arrangement, and states that their whole-arrangement comparison is missing for this recovery result and horizon. Inspect an adequate existing specialist result before commissioning another. Through the profile's `A.15.9` return, request the bounded comparison only when its attainable contribution warrants the complete acquisition burden. The supplier chooses how to produce its result; the adviser retains the recommendation question.

Now add qualified arrangement and security results that cover all three directions. They exclude the specified provider because it cannot preserve the security boundary; internal development remains feasible. A separately qualified probe proposal specifies the remaining question, distinguishing observations, feasible resources, exposure and stops. Compared with immediate commitment, it supports obtaining that information at bounded cost. Using the needed value, uncertainty, consequence and robustness results from `PSDA.6`, `PSDA.7`, `PSDA.8`, `PSDA.9`, `PSDA.14` can recommend considering that probe first while retaining internal development. Those additional premises support the stronger return. They establish neither a throughput effect nor permission to perform the probe.

For a later probe of AI configuration A, `PSDA.15` needs a viable arrangement: an owner can report material changes, competent suppliers can interpret them, and the committee can receive the consequence in time. If observations now concern configuration B while the evaluation still covers A, block advice to extend or deploy B pending the premises needed for that use. Keep the earlier advice about A and an independently supported internal-development claim. An observation notice does not itself choose an operational fallback or revoke permission.

The human branch makes a different missing premise visible. An engineer considering evidence review and interface coordination may have permitted access to review material, yet lack a basis for independent capability and transfer; coordination practice and feedback may also be unavailable. Retain the conditional opportunities. Neither course attendance nor the organization's arrangement comparison supplies those human development results.

### PSDA-ENTRY-03 — Find what is wrong when the report is on time

- **Situation:** Weekly reports arrive on time, yet the planner must telephone colleagues to recover identifiers before using them.
- **Question:** Is the difficulty incomplete information, incompatible identifiers, an unsuitable deadline, or a misleading record?
- **First useful result or blocker:** Distinct formulations with an observation that could separate them, or the exact missing fact that prevents stating what is wrong.
- **Start with:** [PSDA.1](#psda1---generate-plural-problem-formulations) to compare the formulations. If the discrepancy is already understood and only a recording correction is needed, make that correction through the responsible practice.
- **Stop or return:** Stop when the formulation and available facts suffice for the current question. Open a causal-model question only when different explanations change the next useful action; return to the formulation if a check changes what was actually wrong.

The [report-handoff application](#psdaapplication3---app-psd-03--an-on-time-report-that-cannot-yet-be-used) follows that conditional continuation: causal alternatives can inform a bounded answer, while missing evidence, a recipient's objection or later observations can change it. A diagnostic check, temporary operational help and research answer different questions and may occur at the same time.

# Decision Design Principles Framework Architectural Reference

A useful answer can be smaller than the question that first brought people together. “Which pump should we buy?” may first need a distinction between a pump's rated capacity and whether assistance can actually reach the affected people. “What should we develop next?” may first need a worthwhile future contribution rather than a training plan or a model upgrade. Decision Design helps a recipient obtain and use those distinctions without claiming that one discussion, model or recommendation settles the whole situation.

The framework serves practitioners and assisting agents who construct formulations and decision models or arrange a professional engagement, obtain suitable inquiry and analysis, preserve participation conditions and return qualified advice. They may be internal analysts, facilitators working with affected groups, or professionals advising another person or organization. A team can investigate a question for its own later decision while keeping the analysis and choice distinct. The development-direction advising profile adds a distinct recommending performer where that service relationship is the question.

This language also supports the maintenance of the Methods and working arrangements that make this work dependable. Its pattern language offers a repertoire for recurring difficulties. The complete Methods address those difficulties; pattern numbers are addresses, and an actual inquiry selects contributions by the results it needs.

## PSDA.Reference:1 - The field and its useful result

Decision Design constructs inspectable formulations and representations of situations, possible actions, values, uncertainty and consequences. Its characteristic work is to make a difficult question investigable, construct possible responses and the models needed to examine them, and build a warranted comparison where the premises permit one. Its result can be an interpretation, model-use account, alternative set, partial comparison, robustness region or connected answer. These results can complete an inquiry for understanding or contribute to a professional engagement. Arranging participation, composing qualified advice and reconsidering it are parts of the same practice when the receiving use needs them; an external adviser or final choice is not required in every inquiry.

The language does not promise every form of thinking. Mathematical proof, physical explanation, causal identification, research, literary interpretation and engineering design retain their subject Methods. PSDA.11–.15 supply professional engagement, participation, advice and follow-up when needed; the owning practice supplies implementation. Leadership develops feasible joint contributions.

A *pattern* describes a recurring difficulty and a useful way to respond. A *Method* is a reusable way of doing the work; a workshop appointment, diagram or software package is not that way merely because it carries a familiar name. Open the pattern that can change the current answer. If an adequate result already exists, use it within its conditions instead of restarting the inquiry.

Some questions are contested. People can disagree about what is wrong, who bears a consequence, what counts as useful service or which evidence should matter. Preserve differences that change action. Making them explicit does not require every position to have equal evidential support, and a shared sentence does not establish unanimous endorsement.

Other questions are already sufficiently formed. They can enter directly at a missing alternative, specialist premise, comparison or recommendation. A person exploring an opportunity can stop even earlier, without asking another performer for advice.

## PSDA.Reference:2 - How the constructions connect

PSDA.1 develops materially different formulations. Their differences identify evidence needs, intervention mechanisms and consequences a single opening story can hide. PSDA.2 selects and reopens a usable boundary. PSDA.3 constructs complementary models whose claims and omissions fit the question. A model can expose a boundary error, and a changed formulation can make an earlier model unnecessary.

PSDA.4 selects the problem-structuring and analytical Methods that supply the missing contributions. It compares a familiar adequate Method with a combination and qualifies the meaning and conditions of the joins. Combination costs preparation and interpretation; a list of respected techniques supplies no whole Method. Professional participation and facilitation remain direct PSDA.12, PSDA.13 contributions where they are needed.

PSDA.5 constructs a live alternative set. PSDA.6 represents values without inferring weights from the frequency of concerns. When the known menu misses a desired consequence, PSDA.6:4.2 distinguishes ends from proposed means, and PSDA.8:4.2.1 can construct a new means combination backward from the desired conditions and test it forward before returning it to PSDA.5. PSDA.7 connects uncertainty to a claim that could change. PSDA.8 compares consequences under the declared rule, and PSDA.9 examines justified variations and reversals. Their results feed back: a robustness gap can require one missing observation; an omitted consequence can reopen the model or alternative without restarting everything.

B.5.SD makes the connection between supplied claims and the receiving answer itself a working object. This Core Method can use the relevant formulation, model, analytical or professional contribution when it is missing. A source-supported explanation, a proposed experiment and a recommendation have different completion conditions. Construct and examine the inference using the relevant subject Methods and grounds.

[PSDA.20](#psda20---explore-a-situation-through-goals-and-dependencies) supplies one separately usable inquiry through participants' goals and dependencies. It connects the working question, required provision, model views, analysis assumptions and the interpreted answer; an unexpected result can reveal a different problem. PSDA.3 and PSDA.8 remain independently usable model and consequence Methods. Use this whole inquiry only when those connections are part of the missing result.

These are result dependencies and conditional uses, not nineteen compulsory phases. Pattern numbers identify full Methods. The same occasion may enact several Methods, but a claim that they form one composite Method needs explicit whole action, parts, joins and permitted variation under PSDA.4 and FPF B.1.5.

In a professional engagement, formulation and model construction can change which question is worth answering, whose consequences are considered, what counts as the problem and which interventions become plausible. Decision support uses suitably qualified formulations, alternatives, value accounts and evidence to help a receiving decision. A problem formulation can be a complete useful return before a recommendation is possible; a well-formed question can also enter comparison directly.

[PSDA.11](#psda11---bound-the-decision-support-engagement-and-authority-boundary) establishes the receiving use when that use is unclear. [PSDA.12](#psda12---recover-participants-concerns-and-affected-systems-for-a-decision-support-inquiry) supplies attributed concerns and participation limits, while [PSDA.1](#psda1---generate-plural-problem-formulations) shows how rival formulations change evidence needs, boundaries and possible responses. [PSDA.2](#psda2---set-and-reopen-the-problem-boundary) uses the needed engagement and participation results directly, alongside the formulations, to choose a usable inquiry boundary. A formulation alone cannot establish who receives the result or whether an affected person's concern has been represented adequately.

Within that boundary, a model can answer one question and expose another. [PSDA.3](#psda3---construct-complementary-situation-and-option-models) makes the contributions and limits of complementary models usable. [PSDA.4](#psda4---select-problem-structuring-methods-and-combine-them-when-needed) compares the ways of obtaining the needed results and qualifies any combination. [PSDA.13](#psda13---facilitate-decision-support-inquiry-and-preserve-material-dissent) helps participants examine the developing meanings and return shared and contested claims. A corrected concern can therefore change a model or reopen the boundary while independent analysis continues. [PSDA.17](#psda17---reconcile-simultaneous-problem-structuring-and-decision-support-work) becomes useful when the actual interaction between these activities threatens their results.

Formulations and models inform the alternative construction in [PSDA.5](#psda5---generate-decision-alternatives). A consequential difference may then need a value account from [PSDA.6](#psda6---represent-values-and-trade-offs), an uncertainty account from [PSDA.7](#psda7---represent-decision-relevant-uncertainty-and-evidence-limits), a consequence comparison from [PSDA.8](#psda8---compare-consequences-of-decision-alternatives), or the conditions under which a comparison holds or reverses from [PSDA.9](#psda9---test-robustness-and-sensitivity-of-decision-alternatives-and-their-comparison). Obtain only the result that is missing. For example, a sensitivity result can expose a missing road-access premise without requiring another round of alternative generation. A new service concern that the option set cannot address gives a reason to revisit that set or its formulation.

[PSDA.14](#psda14---prepare-and-return-a-decision-support-recommendation) connects the qualified inputs to what the recipient can use now: a direction, a retained set, a conditional comparison, a probe, a request or an abstention with its reason. [PSDA.15](#psda15---arrange-decision-follow-up-or-reassess-advice-after-a-change) connects a material later observation to the advice it can change when follow-up is needed. Neither relation requires performing all preceding patterns. The full [flood-pump application](#psdaapplication1---app-psd-01--a-flood-pump-calculation-is-not-the-whole-investment-answer) shows the connections, including a useful first engagement question and a later whole-investment blocker.

### PSDA.Reference:2.1 - Do we need a model, an explanation, research or advice?

Identify what the recipient lacks. These contributions can be used together, but their completion conditions differ.

| Missing contribution | Useful return and supplying Method |
| --- | --- |
| A representation that makes a relationship inspectable | [PSDA.3](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/DECISION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#psda3---construct-complementary-situation-and-option-models) constructs models for named questions and reconciles only their supported overlaps. A model can expose an unknown without settling it. |
| An answer already available in sources | [RMP.1:4.3](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp143---answer-from-existing-sources-before-starting-a-study) recovers and interprets the relevant material, compares answer-changing alternatives and returns a sufficient answer or precise remaining question. |
| Grounds for an unresolved knowledge claim | [RMP.1](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp1--decide-whether-a-question-needs-research-and-when-to-stop) establishes whether the question requires research; [RMP.2](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp2--choose-a-criticism-bearing-research-design-or-stop) constructs and compares obtainable designs when design selection remains open. |
| A warranted account that the recipient can understand and use | [EXD.1](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd1---establish-and-revise-what-a-recipient-needs-explained) identifies the missing explanatory connection and obtains its subject basis. A missing scientific or mathematical ground returns to that subject work. |
| Professional help with participation, comparison or advice | [PSDA.11](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/DECISION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#psda11---bound-the-decision-support-engagement-and-authority-boundary) bounds the engagement, recipient and choice authority. [PSDA.11–15](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/DPFs/DECISION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#psda11---bound-the-decision-support-engagement-and-authority-boundary) develop these professional contributions. |

A simulation produces a result under a model and its inputs. Establish the model's applicability before relying on that result for the present subject. Conversely, research may produce a defensible model or explanation as its useful result; its worth need not depend on an immediate commercial decision. Routine measurement, restoration of a service and acceptance against an established criterion can finish in their own practices without becoming research.

Use a sufficient existing contribution and stop this selection. If two kinds of work are needed, state what one must return to the other.

## PSDA.Reference:3 - Formulation, professional support and choice

A lone analyst can formulate a question and construct a model for their own understanding. A team can compare alternatives for its later decision. A professional adviser can use the same intellectual results within an engagement. Keep that service's recipient, representation, consent, conflict, confidentiality and authority conditions with their actual professional owner.

PSDA.11 supplies a bounded engagement when one is needed; PSDA.12 recovers affected Systems, attributed concerns and representation limits; PSDA.13 makes participation and challenge workable and the return faithful. Those results can change the intellectual inquiry.
