For a research Method and the knowledge claims that depend on it, use the [research-specific retention and improvement entry](#engineeringreference130---retain-or-improve-a-research-method).


### Engineering.Reference:1.8 - Select and use checklists without losing the work question

Use Core's C.41 checklist family when consequential questions are missed, entries lose their meaning, or local passes leave the shared result uncertain. Choose the contribution needed now; an adequate existing question set, form or answer can be reused.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which questions would reveal a consequential omission? | [FPF C.41 - Select Checklist Questions for a Work Result](../../FPF-Spec.md#c41---select-checklist-questions-for-a-work-result) | A bounded question set with its subjects, grounds and useful coverage. Use one direct question when it suffices; return an unsupported criterion to domain inquiry. |
| Can we adapt or split the form without changing what an answer means? | [FPF C.41.TF - Construct a Checklist Template That Preserves Its Questions](../../FPF-Spec.md#c41tf---construct-a-checklist-template-that-preserves-its-questions) | A reusable form and a filled example whose subject, question, answer and grounds remain recoverable. Retain an existing form that already serves the use. |
| Why is the list skipped, prefilled or used without a needed participant? | [FPF C.41.OF - Fit a Checklist to Its Occasion of Use](../../FPF-Spec.md#c41of---fit-a-checklist-to-its-occasion-of-use) | A usable occasion with access to observations and a truthful response, or the specific missing capability or support to obtain. |
| What can we answer now, and what should change? | [FPF C.41.UA - Use a Checklist to Answer Questions and Act on the Results](../../FPF-Spec.md#c41ua---use-a-checklist-to-answer-questions-and-act-on-the-results) | Supported or unresolved answers and a separate next-action decision. A mismatch may prompt revision of the subject, description or use. Reuse prior answers while their grounds still apply. |
| Do the local answers support the result we need together? | [FPF C.41.SR - Reconcile Checklist Results Across Shared Work](../../FPF-Spec.md#c41sr---reconcile-checklist-results-across-shared-work) | A shared conclusion with its gaps and affected dependencies. Distinguish missing coordination from missing observations; a direct conversation can suffice. |
| Could this criterion or checker miss the difference that matters? | [FPF C.41.QC - Qualify Checklist Criteria and Checking Means](../../FPF-Spec.md#c41qc---qualify-checklist-criteria-and-checking-means) | A bounded qualification, counterexample or unresolved basis for using the check. Reuse a qualification whose conditions still apply. |

The [recurring-omission application (FPF C.41:5.1)](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#c4151---from-a-recurring-omission-to-a-useful-aid) connects question selection and use with [FPF A.3.1.WT's representative trial](../../FPF-Spec.md#a31wt---design-and-interpret-a-method-work-trial) and [FPF C.11.MV's worth comparison](../../FPF-Spec.md#c11mv---compare-the-worth-of-a-method-option). Compare the aid with a simpler sufficient arrangement, including effort moved elsewhere. For shared work, the [workshop application (FPF C.41.SR:5.1)](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#c41sr51---shared-work-with-uncertain-criteria-and-changed-premises) connects local answers with [the shared operating account (OPS.4)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops4---keep-current-operating-state-recoverable-across-participants); a resource conflict still needs a feasible coordination decision.


### Engineering.Reference:1.9 - Obtain and use an aesthetic distinction

A recognizable character, expressive effect or audience response can matter inside another practice. These entries keep obtaining a style distinction and constructing an expressive variant independently available.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What relation makes these works recognizable, and which changes preserve it? | [Obtain a distinction that explains recognizable character](#engineeringreference181---obtain-a-distinction-that-explains-recognizable-character) | A qualified relation, discriminating transformations and their limits, or an explained failure to separate the proposed contributors |
| How can form contribute to the intended experience or activity? | [Construct an expressive variant for the intended use](#engineeringreference182---construct-an-expressive-variant-for-the-intended-use) | A constructible alternative with separate functional, recognition, response and further-use questions, returned to the decision that needs it |
| How does this work in industrial design or narrative stylistics? | [A handle under a functional constraint](#engineeringreference183---industrial-design-a-recognizable-handle-that-still-admits-the-hand); [a narrative transferred to new content](#engineeringreference184---narrative-style-transfer-the-relation-and-expose-an-impossible-separation) | Complete connected cases, including an unavailable manufacturing operation and a failed content/form separation |
| Can an expressive stimulus help distinguish research explanations? | [A discriminating research presentation](#engineeringreference185---expressive-material-as-a-discriminating-research-presentation) | Attainable variants with different predictions, the needed observation and a bounded return to the research claim |
| What happens when expression depends on bodily or temporal relations? | [Bodily and temporal distinctions](#engineeringreference186---bodily-and-temporal-distinctions-in-expressive-action) | A constructible action and separate performer/recipient answers, with a return to the missing movement, observation or capability contribution |

The account applies existing construction, contrast and receiving-use methods. A response to a form does not establish its productive method, general effectiveness or continuing availability.

### Engineering.Reference:1.11 - Model and change the bodily contribution to movement

Use Somatic Movement Modeling with a familiar movement technique and appropriate physical limits, or with a teacher who supplies that support. It connects what the performer experiences, what they can regulate and what the movement actually achieves.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What bodily change might correct this failed part of the movement? | [Model the Bodily Contribution to a Movement (SOM.1)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/SOMATIC-MOVEMENT-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#som1---model-the-bodily-contribution-to-a-movement) | A proposed relation and a small discriminating attempt, or a reason to change an external condition or obtain movement instruction instead. |
| Can the performer distinguish the intended change, and can they regulate it? | [SOM.2](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/SOMATIC-MOVEMENT-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#som2---make-a-bodily-change-distinguishable), then [SOM.3](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/SOMATIC-MOVEMENT-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#som3---regulate-bodily-effort-in-discernible-steps) only if regulation is missing | A bodily contrast the performer can notice again, followed where needed by a controllable increase, reduction or release. Noticing a difference alone does not establish control. |
| Why do available corrections interrupt one another during the whole action? | [Build and Recall a Coordinated Bodily Change (SOM.4)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/SOMATIC-MOVEMENT-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#som4---build-and-recall-a-coordinated-bodily-change) | A combined change to practise and recall, or the contribution that breaks it. Retain a simpler effective task cue when detailed bodily assembly adds nothing useful. |
| Why does coordination fail between two positions that work separately? | [Adapt Bodily Coordination to Changing Support and Load (SOM.5)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/SOMATIC-MOVEMENT-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#som5---adapt-bodily-coordination-to-changing-support-and-load) | A performable portion of the transition, a way to extend and join it in motion, or an identified missing response, cue or observation. Endpoint success does not establish the transition. |

For a correction that works in preparation but disrupts the action, the [COORDINATE example (SOM — COORDINATE — Make a correction work during the whole action)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/SOMATIC-MOVEMENT-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#coordinate--make-a-correction-work-during-the-whole-action) connects modeling, the missing bodily contribution and the return to whole performance. The [writing example (SOM.Reference:3)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/SOMATIC-MOVEMENT-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#somreference3---a-connected-worked-use) follows that route through changing forearm support. These are examples of using several methods, not complete lessons in writing or dance.

HCD supplies learning design, feedback, progression and assessment; RHY supplies rhythmic relations when they matter. SOM supplies the bodily modeling and regulation between those contributions and the receiving technique. A local improvement still has to work with the other actions required at the same time.


### Engineering.Reference:1.12 - Develop a practice or a person's capability

When constituent actions are possible but the whole action fails, examine [what must remain available through the Method vertical](#engineeringreference251---what-must-be-available-through-the-method-vertical). If directing attention to one contribution loses another, follow [continuing the whole action while attention moves](#engineeringreference253---how-can-attention-move-while-the-whole-action-continues).

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which music or dance development work should we choose next? | [Choose the Next Music or Dance Development Work (MDPE.7)](../MUSIC-AND-DANCE-PRACTICE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mdpe7---choose-the-next-music-or-dance-development-work) | A choice, another probe, rejection of the candidates, or a return to a better question, with reasons to revisit it. |
| Is the difficulty in performance, coordination, observation, transmission or the supporting environment? | [Music and Dance Practice Engineering - full pattern index (MDPE — Table of Contents)](../MUSIC-AND-DANCE-PRACTICE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#table-of-contents) | The relevant practice method and an example of its use. |
| What must this person be able to do in later work? | [Derive Human Capability Demand from Representative Later Work (HCD.1)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd1--derive-human-capability-demand-from-representative-later-work) | An evidenced demand, a prospective hypothesis, an outside-HCD return, or the exact missing input. |
| Is the limit a capability, misconception or behaviour, or does something else need to change? | [Diagnose Whether a Capability, Misconception, or Behaviour Limits Work (HCD.3)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd3--diagnose-whether-a-capability-misconception-or-behaviour-limits-work) | A qualified development target, a non-training return, or the observation needed to distinguish them. |
| Which capabilities should be developed or preserved across simultaneous work? | [Architect a Balanced Human Capability Profile Across Simultaneous Work (HCD.4)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd4--architect-a-balanced-human-capability-profile-across-simultaneous-work) | A condition-qualified profile, trade-offs, a recommendation, or an exact blocker. |
| Which feasible development programmes fit this person's later work and resources? | [Compose and Compare Human Capability-Development Programmes for Later Work (HCD.2)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd2---compose-and-compare-human-capability-development-programmes-for-later-work) | A programme comparison for a known person, or a learning-product design return when the future learner is not yet known. |
| Which development method fits the target action and starting evidence? | [Select Human Capability-Development Methods (HCD.5)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd5---select-human-capability-development-methods) | A selected development Method with its fit, risk and evidence needs, or a bounded hold. |
| Which practice task is representative enough to expose the target action and critical errors? | [Design Representative Practice Tasks (HCD.6)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd6---design-representative-practice-tasks) | A task design with target actions, whole-work conditions, feedback opportunities and safety limits. |
| The learner hears the instruction but cannot notice the difference needed for the action. What can we make accessible? | [Help a Learner Discern a Needed Distinction in Practice (HCD.6.1)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd61---help-a-learner-discern-a-needed-distinction-in-practice) | A contrast, a learner response and a next practice action, with the help supplied and the separate execution requirement retained. |
| Which provider, access, tool, AI and environment contributions are actually available? | [Arrange Providers, Access, Tools, and AI Support for Human Capability Development (HCD.7)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd7---arrange-providers-access-tools-and-ai-support-for-human-capability-development) | A support arrangement grounded in actual contributions, access and capacity. |
| Should a missing development contribution be obtained or built? | [Obtain or Build Missing Human Capability-Development Support with Bounded Recursion (HCD.8)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd8---obtain-or-build-missing-human-capability-development-support-with-bounded-recursion) | An obtaining arrangement and operating test for the missing contribution. |
| What happened in this attempt, feedback, correction and retry? | [Perform Deliberate Practice with Feedback (HCD.9)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd9---perform-deliberate-practice-with-feedback) | A traceable practice episode and the next justified attempt. |
| Should task, timing, retrieval, mixing or challenge conditions change next, and how? | [Choose Whether and How to Vary, Space, Interleave, or Progress Practice (HCD.10)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd10---choose-whether-and-how-to-vary-space-interleave-or-progress-practice) | A bounded progression decision tied to practice history and intended later conditions. |
| What did this person contribute in representative work? | [Assess Human Performance in Representative Work (HCD.11)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd11--assess-human-performance-in-representative-work) | A bounded performance and capability conclusion with its conditions and limits. |
| Does the contribution transfer to unfamiliar work, or can this person learn from a new source? | [Test Transfer to Unfamiliar Work or Learning from a New Source (HCD.12)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd12--test-transfer-to-unfamiliar-work-or-learning-from-a-new-source) | A transfer or new-source-learning conclusion, an adaptation need, or the evidence needed to decide. |
| What remains after a delay, and what depends on tools or support? | [Test Human Capability Retention and Dependence on Tools or Other Support (HCD.13)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd13--test-human-capability-retention-and-dependence-on-tools-or-other-support) | Separate retention and support-dependence conclusions. |
| Which development component should change from the evidence? | [Revise the Human Capability-Development Arrangement from Evidence (HCD.14)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd14--revise-the-human-capability-development-arrangement-from-evidence) | A bounded revision and the observation that will test it. |
| How should development continue when later work or evidence changes? | [Sustain Continuing Human Capability Development (HCD.15)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd15--sustain-continuing-human-capability-development) | A holder-specific continuing-development arrangement with triggers and returns. |
| What does the evidence support for this HCD Method, and should its use change? | [Keep Human Capability-Development Method Claims Current (HCD.16)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd16--keep-human-capability-development-method-claims-current) | A supported limited use, a narrowed claim, an unresolved comparison or a protection stop for the named HCD use. A justified change can adopt, revise, branch or retire a use; further inquiry is selected only for a worthwhile obtainable contribution. |
| Which HCD cultural relation should a bounded population continue or change? | [Deliberately Continue and Change Human Capability-Development Culture (HCD.17)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd17--deliberately-continue-and-change-human-capability-development-culture) | A supported decision about continuing or changing the practice, with the limits of the available evidence; later observation when the selected inquiry or a claimed later result requires it. |
| Which individual or group arrangement fits the intended learning actions and actual resources? | [Compose and Compare Arrangements for Individual and Group Learning (HCD.20)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd20---compose-and-compare-arrangements-for-individual-and-group-learning) | Comparable arrangements with complete participant and provider burdens, available help and personal learning actions retained. |
| Who can form a workable learning group, and how should membership change? | [Form and Change Learning Work Groups (HCD.21)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd21---form-and-change-learning-work-groups) | A compatible grouping with contact, preparation, participation and recovery conditions. |
| What must each learner contribute to a shared task? | [Design Shared Learning Tasks with Necessary Individual Contributions (HCD.22)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd22---design-shared-learning-tasks-with-necessary-individual-contributions) | A shared task linking personal actions, mutual dependencies, feedback and material transfers. |
| How can explaining and comparing solutions develop personal reasoning? | [Learn through Explanation and Comparison of Solutions (HCD.23)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd23---learn-through-explanation-and-comparison-of-solutions) | An explanation and comparison task followed by a personal application, with supplied help visible. |
| How can peer review teach judgement and revision? | [Learn Evaluation and Revision through Peer Review (HCD.24)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd24---learn-evaluation-and-revision-through-peer-review) | An arrangement in which reviewers apply criteria and authors judge feedback and revise, with qualified help for unresolved disagreement. |
| How can comparing projects develop transfer? | [Learn Transfer through Comparison of Projects (HCD.25)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd25---learn-transfer-through-comparison-of-projects) | A supported relation across projects, a condition that breaks it, and a learner's application to a new case. |
| How should a group respond when its shared learning stalls? | [Regulate Shared Learning (HCD.26)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd26---regulate-shared-learning) | A process change or prompt fitted to the difficulty, and a check of how participants use it and what changes. |
| How can personal learning routes fit shared meetings and material transfers? | [Coordinate Personal Learning Routes with a Shared Rhythm (HCD.27)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd27---coordinate-personal-learning-routes-with-a-shared-rhythm) | Feasible connections between individual work, shared occasions, help and personal return windows. |
| How can we construct a whole learning product before its learners are known? | [Construct and Revise a Whole Learning Product for a Future Audience (HCD.28)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd28---construct-and-revise-a-whole-learning-product-for-a-future-audience) | Whole-product alternatives for a future audience, with missing subject, teaching or supply contributions identified. |

Use HCD.16 to complete the appraisal with the conclusion supported by the available evidence. Undertake a further inquiry when its attainable contribution warrants the full burden for learners and providers. If a comparison is unavailable, leave the claim that requires it unresolved.

The [Human Capability Development DPF (HCD — Table of Contents)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#table-of-contents) contains 29 patterns: HCD.1–HCD.17 and nested HCD.6.1 address personal development; HCD.18–HCD.19 address instructional-material evaluation; HCD.20–HCD.27 construct and support individual and shared learning arrangements; and HCD.28 connects these contributions into a whole learning product for a future audience. A pattern supplies guidance and a result form; it does not establish that development work occurred, capability changed, a provider operated, or an authorized person made a programme, employment or release decision.


### Engineering.Reference:1.13 - Evaluate instructional material for its intended use

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How should we judge a worksheet, explanation or learning route for its intended readers? | [Select or Construct a Characterization and Evaluation Specification for Instructional Material (HCD.18)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd18---select-or-construct-a-characterization-and-evaluation-specification-for-instructional-material) | A compatible evaluation specification, or a new one tying the audience's tasks and allowed help to criteria, evidence and the use or repair decision. Use HCD.19 directly when a compatible specification already exists. Stop construction with the usable specification or a precise unresolved criterion. |
| Does this material support the reader's task, and what needs repair? | [Evaluate Instructional Material through Representative Reader Work and Diagnose Its Repair (HCD.19)](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd19---evaluate-instructional-material-through-representative-reader-work-and-diagnose-its-repair) | A supported material contribution, a limiting defect with its affected reach, or a specific criterion or evidence gap. Start with a compatible specification; use HCD.18 only if it is absent or unsuitable. Keep prior knowledge and later help visible when interpreting the first response. Stop at the supported use or repair conclusion. |

These two methods judge instructional material. For a person's performance, transfer or retention, use HCD.11–HCD.13 above. An ordinary professional reference is evaluated for its lookup use unless it also promises instruction.


### Engineering.Reference:1.14 - Make an explanation understandable and usable

Use Explanation Design when someone needs to follow a connection and use it: why an outcome occurred, how a derivation works, or why a recommendation follows from its grounds. Start with the question that is unresolved now.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which question should this explanation answer, and has the recipient changed it? | [Establish and Revise What a Recipient Needs Explained (EXD.1)](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd1---establish-and-revise-what-a-recipient-needs-explained) | The needed connection, its conditions and intended use, with any subject input still missing. Use an already clear question directly. |
| What supports the connection we are trying to explain? | [Obtain and Carry the Subject Explanation (EXD.Reference:3)](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exdreference3---obtain-and-carry-the-subject-explanation) | The relevant derivation, causal grounds or recommendation rationale, with its conditions; or the exact question that the subject practice still needs to answer. Retain a useful conditional answer while obtaining that input. |
| How can an example make a rule usable, and where does its correspondence stop? | [Build and Bound an Explanatory Example (EXD.2)](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd2---build-and-bound-an-explanatory-example) | A worked instance, its correspondence to the claim and a changed condition that shows the limit of that use. |
| How should the text, formula and diagram work together? | [Coordinate the Expression of an Explanation (EXD.3)](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd3---coordinate-the-expression-of-an-explanation) | One sufficient form or a coordinated combination through which the recipient can follow the selected relation. Obtain a missing premise or derivation before treating its absence as a presentation problem. |
| How should the recipient's response change the next explanation? | [Co-Construct and Repair an Explanation in Dialogue (EXD.4)](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd4---co-construct-and-repair-an-explanation-in-dialogue) | A recovered relation, revised question, the premise or choice on which participants disagree, or a request for missing subject input. Close the exchange when the receiving need is met. |
| A learner can repeat the formula but uses the wrong relation. What would help? | [Guide a Recipient's Own Explanation (EXD.5)](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd5---guide-a-recipients-own-explanation) | The learner's initial explanation, targeted feedback and another attempt at applying the relation, with the help used for each attempt stated. Use a later task when retention or independent use is the question. |
| Should we keep this explanation or make a particular repair? | [Compare Explanations for the Recipient's Use and Decide Whether a Repair Is Worthwhile (EXD.6)](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#exd6---compare-explanations-for-the-recipients-use-and-decide-whether-a-repair-is-worthwhile) | A repair worth its burden, a qualified provisional choice, or a sufficient explanation to retain for this recipient and use. Distinguish a change of content, expression or assistance when comparing the result. |

The [EXD — Use profiles](../EXPLANATION-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#use-profiles) adapt these methods to instruction, technical and advisory work, and human–AI interaction. For evaluation of instructional material as a whole, use the HCD.18 and HCD.19 entries above. A learner's later performance, transfer or retention calls for the corresponding HCD method and its conditions.


### Engineering.Reference:1.15 - Keep an operation working

Use the [Operations Management DPF (OPS — Table of Contents)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#table-of-contents) when the current question concerns continuing work, admission, cases, priority, queues, constraints, capacity, service, operating evidence, quality, simultaneous work, method improvement, cultural continuation, meaningful aims or performance interpretation.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which operation, commitments, subjects and flow units should orient the decision? | [Identify the Operating System, Commitments, and Flow Units (OPS.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops1---identify-the-operating-system-commitments-and-flow-units) | A bounded operating-system and commitment account. |
| Which project, process, case, queueing, control or mixed views and coordination Methods answer the current questions? | [Select Work-Management Views and Coordination Methods (OPS.2)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops2---select-work-management-views-and-coordination-methods) | A justified choice of views and coordination Methods for the current questions, including keeping the existing arrangement when it suffices. |
| Which subjects and relations sit behind cases, queues, resources and records? | [Distinguish Operating Subjects, Cases, Queues, Resources, and Records (OPS.3)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops3---distinguish-operating-subjects-cases-queues-resources-and-records) | A typed operating-subject account that prevents record or queue labels from replacing the work. |
| Which qualified current claims let participants decide, resume and coordinate? | [Keep Current Operating State Recoverable Across Participants (OPS.4)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops4---keep-current-operating-state-recoverable-across-participants) | A shared current-state account with source, time and uncertainty visible. |
| Which eligible demand may enter now under bounded start conditions? | [Admit Work and Limit Starts (OPS.5)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops5---admit-work-and-limit-starts) | An admission, deferral or stop with explicit start limits. |
| What work may happen next in this admitted case? | [Continue Cases and Handle Exceptions (OPS.6)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops6---continue-cases-and-handle-exceptions) | A justified continuation or exception disposition. |
| Does aging, urgency or consequence evidence revise current priority or a commitment? | [Manage Aging, Urgency, and Service Commitments (OPS.7)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops7---manage-aging-urgency-and-service-commitments) | A bounded priority or commitment revision with authority and evidence. |
| What is ready for which service, and what should release and protection policy control? | [Coordinate Queues and Buffers (OPS.8)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops8---coordinate-queues-and-buffers) | A queue, release and buffer policy or the missing sizing input. |
| Can new work start while an earlier job may return for correction? | [Choose Work-Release Rules When Earlier Work Can Return (OPS.8.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops81---choose-work-release-rules-when-earlier-work-can-return) | A release rule that accounts for remaining work and possible returns, with an executable response when feedback arrives. |
| Can reserved capacity be used for other useful work and still return in time? | [Use Protective Capacity While Keeping It Available (OPS.8.2)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops82---use-protective-capacity-while-keeping-it-available) | A choice of auxiliary work and an interruption, resource-release and restoration arrangement that preserves the required service. |
| What currently limits completion, and which change is supported after comparing competing explanations? | [Diagnose and Treat the Current Operating Constraint (OPS.9)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops9---diagnose-and-treat-the-current-operating-constraint) | A supported constraint treatment or a discriminating probe. |
| What fits usable resource windows under variability? | [Qualify Operating Capacity Under Variability (OPS.10)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops10---qualify-operating-capacity-under-variability) | A feasible timetable, a demonstrated capacity shortfall, or a qualified service forecast. |
| How would a change of service, arrivals or resource access affect completion and waiting? | [Construct and Compare Operating Capacity Models (OPS.10.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops101---construct-and-compare-operating-capacity-models) | A calculation for particular jobs, average waiting or a service probability, with the assumptions needed to use its result. |
| How can these jobs meet their deadline with shared resources and calendar gaps? | [Construct and Revise a Feasible Deadline Schedule (OPS.10.2)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops102---construct-and-revise-a-feasible-deadline-schedule) | A feasible schedule or a reason the deadline cannot be met; feasible start times and a revised plan when conditions change. |
| Which coupling can defeat a local plan, and which decisions must be coordinated? | [Coordinate Interacting Operating Structures (OPS.11)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops11---coordinate-interacting-operating-structures) | A dependency account and compatible decisions from the responsible participants. |
| How do resource use, activity completion and order completion fit in one operating model? | [Construct and Reconcile Operating Models Across Scales (OPS.11.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops111---construct-and-reconcile-operating-models-across-scales) | A model that retains shared resources, required joins and the conditions that can change the plan. |
| Which feasible intervention protects affected people and still supports the service? | [Protect Human Conditions in Operating Decisions (OPS.12)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops12---protect-human-conditions-in-operating-decisions) | A bounded operating intervention with protected human conditions and evidence needs. |
| What service can authorized parties agree under actual resources and conditions? | [Align Commitments, Resources, and Service Outcomes (OPS.13)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops13---align-commitments-resources-and-service-outcomes) | A credible service commitment or an exact hold. |
| Which throughput, cash, payment and receipt differences change the choice? | [Relate Throughput, Cash, and Operating Consequences (OPS.14)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops14---relate-throughput-cash-and-operating-consequences) | A comparison of operating and financial consequences without collapsing them. |
| Which observations and meanings support this operating decision? | [Build a Decision-Specific Operating Account (OPS.15)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops15---build-a-decision-specific-operating-account) | A decision-specific account with source and interpretation limits. |
| How should events be counted and timed when cases overlap, return, cancel or remain unfinished? | [Derive Operating Quantities from Events (OPS.15.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops151---derive-operating-quantities-from-events) | Waiting, occupancy and output quantities on compatible populations and observation windows. |
| What evidence supports adopting, revising, branching or stopping this operating Method? | [Decide Whether and How to Change an Operating Method (OPS.16)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops16---decide-whether-and-how-to-change-an-operating-method) | A bounded disposition of the admitted Method or a revised candidate account, with the supported use and evidence limits. |
| Which operating moves fit this work family, and what change reopens their use? | [Compare and Refresh Operations Methods (OPS.17)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops17---compare-and-refresh-operations-methods) | A compared and current operations-method repertoire for the stated use. |
| What continuation, acceptance, containment or recovery action does the evidence support? | [Control Operating Quality and Reliability (OPS.18)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops18---control-operating-quality-and-reliability) | A quality or reliability response with exact evidence and stop conditions. |
| Which cross-scale reconfiguration preserves the simultaneous operating results that matter? | [Reconcile Simultaneous Operating Work Across Cases and Scales (OPS.19)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops19---reconcile-simultaneous-operating-work-across-cases-and-scales) | A cross-scale continuation, reconfiguration or explicit unresolved conflict. |
| Which Operations practice should this population continue or change? | [Deliberately Continue and Change Operations Culture (OPS.20)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops20---deliberately-continue-and-change-operations-culture) | A supported decision about continuing or changing the practice; further observation only when its attainable contribution justifies the effort. |
| What useful improvement should the operation pursue, and how should it be compared? | [Choose Operating Aims, Targets and Comparisons (OPS.21)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops21---choose-operating-aims-targets-and-comparisons) | A meaningful aim and comparison, a first action, or a justified decision to monitor without a numerical target. |
| How should a result be judged when ambition, conditions and joint work differ? | [Interpret Operating Performance and Decide the Response (OPS.22)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops22---interpret-operating-performance-and-decide-the-response) | A reasoned operating assessment, its uncertainty and an effective response under the actual authority. |

The [archive case](#engineeringreference9---how-can-two-archive-services-share-staff-without-losing-their-commitments) combines only the OPS contributions needed for one allocation question. The remaining patterns are available for their own working conditions; their availability does not add them silently to that case.


### Engineering.Reference:1.16 - Explain resource use, costs and operating accounts

Management Accounting helps a controller, accountant or manager explain how work uses resources and how that use appears in money, forecasts and performance accounts. It also uses economic requirements to develop changes to the product, process and provision together with their responsible disciplines. Select the needed account, forecast, activity design or use of information from the engineering question; a small model of the relevant work can be sufficient.

| Working question | Start with | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What resources will the proposed work consume, and what will they cost? | [Build the Resource-Consumption and Cost Model (MA.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma1---build-the-resource-consumption-and-cost-model) | A resource-consumption and cost model with the detail needed for the operating decision. |
| Do released hours mean available capacity or lower payments? | [Explain the Cost and Use of Capacity (MA.2)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma2---explain-the-cost-and-use-of-capacity) | An account distinguishing paid capacity, usable capacity, reserve and payment consequences. |
| How should shared costs be assigned for this use? | [Assign Shared Costs for the Stated Use (MA.3)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma3---assign-shared-costs-for-the-stated-use) | An allocation suited to the stated use, with its tracing and capacity assumptions. |
| Why do operating results, reported profit and cash differ? | [Reconcile Operating, Reporting and Cash Accounts (MA.4)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma4---reconcile-operating-reporting-and-cash-accounts) | A reconciliation that preserves the meaning of operating, reporting and cash accounts. |
| How should the operating forecast change with demand or supply? | [Construct and Update an Operating Forecast (MA.5)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma5---construct-and-update-an-operating-forecast) | An updated forecast with its assumptions, scenarios and consequential supply thresholds. |
| Is this number a forecast, a target, a request or an authorization? | [Separate Forecasts, Targets and Resource Requests (MA.6)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma6---separate-forecasts-targets-and-resource-requests) | Separate expectations, targets and resource requests, with the authorized amount distinguished. |
| What explains this cost or margin difference? | [Explain a Cost or Margin Difference (MA.7)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma7---explain-a-cost-or-margin-difference) | An explanation that separates volume, mix, usage and price contributions, with limits on causal claims. |
| How do customer or product economics change over time? | [Account for Customer and Product Economics Over Time (MA.8)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma8---account-for-customer-and-product-economics-over-time) | An account of acquisition, retention, support and scale over the relevant horizon; finance supplies a needed valuation. |
| How should accounting information be used in decisions and coordination, and what behavior does that use encourage? | [Design and Examine the Use of Management Accounting Information (MA.9)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma9---design-and-examine-the-use-of-management-accounting-information) | A proposed or revised use connected to decisions, authority and timing, with its effects on joint work examined. |
| Which changes to the offering, product, process and provision could meet this economic requirement? | [Develop an Activity Design from an Economic Requirement (MA.10)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma10---develop-an-activity-design-from-an-economic-requirement) | An economically examined activity design with related resource, payment and performance conditions. |

[Operations Management (OPS)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) uses these accounts for operating comparisons. A forecast can inform a resource decision while the authorization remains a separate result. The [repair cooperative case](#engineeringreference7---how-should-we-set-a-target-and-judge-a-miss-after-conditions-change) connects these accounts to the construction of a meaningful aim and later performance interpretation through OPS.21–22.


### Engineering.Reference:1.17 - Model financial positions and effects

Financial Domain Modeling helps a financial practitioner, business modeler or service designer establish whose financial position a model describes, what events can change it and how a service contributes to a participant's result. Its five methods connect parties, rights and obligations, contractual flows, actual effects and service use.

| Working question | Start with | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What financial position does this record describe? | [Recover the Financial Position Behind a Record (FDM.1)](../FINANCIAL-DOMAIN-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fdm1---recover-the-financial-position-behind-a-record) | The relevant rights, duties and record claims for the stated party. |
| Which party or group has this financial position? | [Choose Party and Group Boundaries for Financial Modeling (FDM.2)](../FINANCIAL-DOMAIN-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fdm2---choose-party-and-group-boundaries-for-financial-modeling) | Boundaries that distinguish the debtor, entity or group and the cash it can use. |
| Which contractual events and payments can follow? | [Derive Events and Conditional Flows from Financial Contract Terms (FDM.3)](../FINANCIAL-DOMAIN-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fdm3---derive-events-and-conditional-flows-from-financial-contract-terms) | A schedule of contractual events and conditional flows, distinguished from actual flows. |
| What did the approval, posting or payment actually change? | [Establish What a Financial Action Changed (FDM.4)](../FINANCIAL-DOMAIN-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fdm4---establish-what-a-financial-action-changed) | The established financial effect and any remaining obligation under the applicable rules. |
| How does this financial service help the participant? | [Trace a Financial Service to a Participant's Result (FDM.5)](../FINANCIAL-DOMAIN-MODELING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fdm5---trace-a-financial-service-to-a-participants-result) | A connection from the service output to its use and the participant's result, such as admission or financial benefit. |

Use [Semantic Integration Engineering (SIE)](SEMANTIC-INTEGRATION-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) when separately governed meanings or identities need reconciliation. Financial Domain Modeling supplies the financial interpretation; the relevant decision practice uses it.


### Engineering.Reference:1.18 - Value investments, arrange finance and manage liquidity

[Corporate Finance (FIN)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) provides methods for valuing investments, arranging finance, preserving liquidity and managing financial exposure. It also explains the financial relations of the activity and constructs financing terms and connections between group entities. The resulting claims and payment paths return to the investment and operating choices they enable.

Choose the question you need to answer, then open the linked method and check its conditions of use.

**Part A - Cash and decision accounts**

| Working question | Start with | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What financial choice are we making, for which corporation and time horizon? | [Frame the Corporate Finance Decision, Corporation, Jurisdiction, and Time (FIN.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin1---frame-the-corporate-finance-decision-corporation-jurisdiction-and-time) | A usable financial question, with the corporation, time horizon and constraints identified. |
| Will money be available when payments fall due? | [Assess Liquidity and Funding Needs by Date (FIN.2)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin2---assess-liquidity-and-funding-needs-by-date) | A dated cash forecast and any funding requirement at the relevant payment dates. |
| How can stock, collections or payment terms improve cash availability? | [Manage Working Capital and Cash Conversion (FIN.3)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin3---manage-working-capital-and-cash-conversion) | A comparison of working-capital changes with their operating and commercial consequences. |
| Which accounts and forecasts does this financial decision need? | [Prepare Accounts and Forecasts for the Finance Decision (FIN.4)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin4---prepare-accounts-and-forecasts-for-the-finance-decision) | The required financial view, with material differences between the supplied accounts reconciled. |

**Part B - Investment and value**

| Working question | Start with | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What cost-of-capital estimate matches the cash flows being valued? | [Estimate Cost of Capital and Financing Constraints (FIN.5)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin5---estimate-cost-of-capital-and-financing-constraints) | A required-return estimate matched to the cash flows and claims in the valuation. |
| What does this capital project add compared with its alternative? | [Value Capital Projects (FIN.6)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin6---value-capital-projects) | Incremental project cash flows and their value on matching valuation grounds. |
| What is this asset, business or ownership interest worth? | [Value Assets and the Corporation (FIN.7)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin7---value-assets-and-the-corporation) | A valuation of the identified asset or claim at the stated date, with its assumptions and limits. |
| What is the value of being able to wait, expand or abandon? | [Value Financial and Real Options (FIN.8)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin8---value-financial-and-real-options) | A value for the specified option under its exercise, uncertainty and financing conditions. |
| Which investments, acquisition or divestment should we compare under limited capital? | [Compare Capital Investments and Allocations (FIN.9)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin9---compare-capital-investments-and-allocations) | A comparison of feasible capital allocations, their interactions and incremental value. |

**Part C - Financing, distributions and recovery**

| Working question | Start with | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which financing contributions and terms can meet the need and be acceptable to their participants? | [Design Financing Instruments and Terms (FIN.10)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin10---design-financing-instruments-and-terms) | A constructed or compared proposal with net proceeds, future service, rights, participant consequences and conditions for funding. |
| How should financing and support connect the group's entities? | [Construct Financing Arrangements Across Group Entities (FIN.23)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin23---construct-financing-arrangements-across-group-entities) | A financial arrangement with entity cash paths, internal and external claims, loss consequences and transition conditions. |
| What mix of debt and equity is feasible and useful? | [Select Capital Structure (FIN.11)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin11---select-capital-structure) | A proposed financing mix compared under cash, tax, control, access and distress conditions. |
| Could covenants or refinancing remove access to funds? | [Preserve Covenant Headroom and Financing Flexibility (FIN.12)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin12---preserve-covenant-headroom-and-financing-flexibility) | The applicable covenant or funding test, remaining headroom and available responses. |
| How much capital should we retain or return to owners? | [Decide How Much Capital to Retain or Return (FIN.21)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin21---decide-how-much-capital-to-retain-or-return) | A comparison of retention, dividends or repurchases, with an amount and form supported by the funding conditions. |
| What recovery routes remain when ordinary repayment is inadequate? | [Compare Financial Restructuring and Recovery Routes (FIN.22)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin22---compare-financial-restructuring-and-recovery-routes) | A comparison of viable restructuring routes and the recoveries of affected claimants. |

**Part D - Exposure and treasury action**

| Working question | Start with | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How would changes in prices, rates, payments or funding access affect the corporation? | [Identify and Measure Financial Exposures (FIN.13)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin13---identify-and-measure-financial-exposures) | A financial exposure traced to the relevant claims and operations, with its decision-relevant consequences. |
| Should we hedge or transfer this financial exposure? | [Decide Whether and How to Hedge or Transfer Financial Risk (FIN.14)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin14---decide-whether-and-how-to-hedge-or-transfer-financial-risk) | A comparison of protection, cost, residual risk and cash demands. |
| How do we carry out and verify this permitted treasury action? | [Execute Treasury and Liquidity Decisions (FIN.15)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin15---execute-treasury-and-liquidity-decisions) | The verified financial effect of the selected action, or the execution problem still to resolve. |

**Part E - Advice, renewal and continuing practice**

| Working question | Start with | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How do we turn financial analysis into usable advice? | [Prepare a Finance Recommendation and Return It for a Decision (FIN.16)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin16---prepare-a-finance-recommendation-and-return-it-for-a-decision) | A recommended financial move with its reasons, assumptions and conditions. |
| What must be updated after a financial premise changes? | [Refresh Financial Models and Data (FIN.17)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin17---refresh-financial-models-and-data) | The affected model, projection or conclusion updated for its use, or a supported decision to leave it unchanged. |
| Should we retain or change the method used for this financial question? | [Choose Whether and How to Change Corporate-Finance Methods (FIN.18)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin18---choose-whether-and-how-to-change-corporate-finance-methods) | A choice among method variants based on the financial result they can improve and the effort required. |
| How do we reconcile conflicting investment, financing and treasury commitments? | [Reconcile Simultaneous Corporate-Finance Work Across Claims and Horizons (FIN.19)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin19---reconcile-simultaneous-corporate-finance-work-across-claims-and-horizons) | A shared account of cash and commitments, or a comparison of needed changes to the work arrangement. |
| How can useful financial practices continue or harmful routines change? | [Deliberately Continue and Change Corporate-Finance Culture (FIN.20)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-FINANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#fin20---deliberately-continue-and-change-corporate-finance-culture) | A continuation or change decision informed by how the practice is learned, selected and retained. |

For questions about costs or operating accounts, use the [management-accounting questions](#engineeringreference116---explain-resource-use-costs-and-operating-accounts). For the parties, rights or contractual flows behind a financial result, use the [financial-modeling questions](#engineeringreference117---model-financial-positions-and-effects).


### Engineering.Reference:1.19 - Coordinate economic plans, exchanges and shared resources

Economic Reasoning and Coordination connects calculation, exchange construction, commitments and institutional change. It uses existing financial and operating results while adding the questions about how participants' plans, choices and constraints affect one another.

| Working question | Start with | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What do the prices or weights in this calculation actually support? | [Recover the Basis for an Economic Calculation (ECO.1)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco1---recover-the-basis-for-an-economic-calculation) | A grounded comparison or a conditional choice which preserves the missing exchange or resource condition. |
| Should this changed price alter our use of a resource? | [Reconsider Resource Use in Response to Price Signals (ECO.2)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco2---reconsider-resource-use-in-response-to-price-signals) | A feasible adjustment or reason to keep the plan, with the relevant scope and transition costs. |
| Can different plans be joined into a useful exchange? | [Discover an Exchange between Different Plans (ECO.3)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco3---discover-an-exchange-between-different-plans) | A proposed combination of contributions and terms, or the specific incompatibility. |
| How can a venture begin when commitments depend on one another? | [Form Resource Commitments for an Uncertain Venture (ECO.4)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco4---form-resource-commitments-for-an-uncertain-venture) | An attainable first action or joint commitment with available resources and remaining exposure. |
| Which terms make hidden quality or effort matter to the participant? | [Choose Exchange Terms for Private Information and Effort (ECO.5)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco5---choose-exchange-terms-for-private-information-and-effort) | An incentive and participation comparison with usable payment, observation or warranty conditions. |
| How will trading partners adapt after a dedicated investment? | [Arrange Adaptation in a Dependent Trading Relationship (ECO.6)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco6---arrange-adaptation-in-a-dependent-trading-relationship) | A feasible technical, contractual or organizational arrangement for the named dependence and disturbance. |
| How can several users sustain a shared resource? | [Coordinate Use and Renewal of a Shared Resource (ECO.7)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco7---coordinate-use-and-renewal-of-a-shared-resource) | Workable use, upkeep, observation and adaptation rules with their available contributions. |
| Why does a rule fail when moved between close cooperation and wider exchange? | [Join Direct Cooperation with a Wider Economic Order (ECO.8)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco8---join-direct-cooperation-with-a-wider-economic-order) | A correction to the affected interaction, preserving the different conditions of coordination. |
| Should an inherited economic rule be retained or changed, and how? | [Decide Whether and How to Change Economic Rules through Their Working Practices (ECO.9)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco9---decide-whether-and-how-to-change-economic-rules-through-their-working-practices) | A supported change, bounded trial, retained rule or limitation, including the practices and capabilities needed. |
| Will lower resource use per result reduce total use? | [Trace Efficiency Savings through Demand Responses (Rebound Effects) (ECO.10)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco10---trace-efficiency-savings-through-demand-responses-rebound-effects) | A comparison with and without induced responses, or a useful threshold with its scope and limits. |

For a new service, the [connected venture example (ECO — ECO-VENTURE - Turn a useful idea into a feasible service arrangement)](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco-venture---turn-a-useful-idea-into-a-feasible-service-arrangement) joins discovering an exchange, recovering its economic grounds, forming commitments and arranging adaptation. If tooling becomes reusable and another supplier is available, the dependence changes; ordinary purchasing can then suffice. A supplier's separately performed work is linked by an agreement, while interpreting that agreement can be a constituent operation in the buyer's venture work.


### Engineering.Reference:1.20 - Model dependence, spread and protective action

Use Defense and Transmission Modeling when a practice or variant keeps spreading, changes the conditions of its own continuation, or provokes a response whose consequences are unclear. Begin with the affected work and participants. A biological analogy does not establish the mechanism of an engineering or cultural case.

| Working question | Open | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does continued use help the work, and what would be lost if the support disappeared? | [Distinguish Dependence, Cooperation and Parasitic Use (DTM.1)](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm1---distinguish-dependence-cooperation-and-parasitic-use) | A comparison of continuation, dependence and consequences for the named participants, with unresolved effects retained. |
| Why does a practice spread, stall or return after suppression? | [DTM.2](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm2---build-a-transmission-law-from-exposure-and-uptake), [DTM.3](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm3---couple-change-within-carriers-to-spread-between-them) and [DTM.4](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm4---find-conditions-for-variant-invasion-persistence-and-return) | A law distinguishing exposure, uptake and reconstruction, connected to participant change and the conditions for continuation or return. |
| Does a changing aggregate reflect selection, interaction or diversion of a shared mechanism? | [DTM.5](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm5---separate-selection-within-and-among-collectives), [DTM.6](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm6---model-competition-and-facilitation-between-variants) or [DTM.7](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm7---locate-diversion-of-a-shared-control-or-cooperation-mechanism) | The applicable decomposition or causal construction; a statistical contribution is kept separate from its explanation. |
| Which protective action changes the needed result, including harm or lost capability caused by the response? | [DTM.8](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm8---compare-protective-actions-against-continuing-or-spreading-activity-by-target-and-remaining-effects) and [DTM.9](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm9---model-damage-and-feedback-from-protective-responses-to-continuing-or-spreading-activity) | A comparison of action targets and response feedback, preserving residual activity, capacity, memory and effects on other participants. |

Use the [connected DTM entries (DTM — Defense and Transmission Modeling DPF Readme)](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#defense-and-transmission-modeling-dpf-readme) when several of these results are needed together. The [review-capacity example](#engineeringreference15---can-protective-review-work-with-the-capacity-we-have) shows why a modeled protective effect still needs an operating contribution.


### Engineering.Reference:1.21 - Continue and change a shared practice

A working method may become easier to copy while the ability to explain, alter or teach it becomes harder to obtain. Or a capable group may reasonably decline a proposed change. Begin with the work and the contribution that could make a difference.

**Find what the next work needs → compare learning and support → trace wider use → choose a feasible continuation → observe use → keep methods available for further development.**

[FPF C.36.RP](../../FPF-Spec.md#c36rp---sustain-and-renew-shared-ways-of-working) locates the unavailable contribution and compares learning, help, tools and changed arrangements. [HCD.13](../Human%20Capability%20Engineering%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd13--test-human-capability-retention-and-dependence-on-tools-or-other-support) distinguishes human retention from support dependence when that question matters. [DTM.2](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm2---build-a-transmission-law-from-exposure-and-uptake) and [DTM.3](../DEFENSE-AND-TRANSMISSION-MODELING-DPF.md#dtm3---couple-change-within-carriers-to-spread-between-them) connect what another participant obtains with subsequent transmission; reconstruction can produce a useful variant.

Use [FPF A.3.1.MI](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/FPF-Spec.md#a31mi---introduce-a-method-into-practice-and-decide-what-to-keep-or-change) to separate a changed method from a changed way of introducing it, and [ECO.7](../ECONOMIC-REASONING-AND-COORDINATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eco7---coordinate-use-and-renewal-of-a-shared-resource) when different participants must sustain a constrained support contribution. Return changed results to the method, learning, support or selection decision they affect. A supported decision to keep the current practice is a complete result.

The [shared-method example](#engineeringreference17---how-can-we-share-a-method-without-losing-the-means-to-develop-it) follows these dependencies.



### Engineering.Reference:1.22 - Build a useful cultural or community contribution

Start with the change people need. A discussion group, a useful resource, learning and a dependable service can call for different contributions. The [CB — Community Management Readme](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#community-management-readme) offers three practical entries; its [CB — Community Management Principles Framework Architectural Reference](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#community-management-principles-framework-architectural-reference) explains how to connect the methods. People may also develop and use a practice independently.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Would a community help, or would a resource, learning or a dependable service serve people better? | [Choose a Useful Cultural or Community Contribution (CB.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb1---choose-a-useful-cultural-or-community-contribution) | An understandable proposal for who could benefit, what each participant would contribute and which first action could test it; an adequate existing route may be sufficient. |
| How can one request lead to useful help? | [Arrange the First Useful Exchanges (CB.2)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb2---arrange-the-first-useful-exchanges) | A completed exchange, a known use or remaining gap, and a feasible continuation. |
| How can someone join, change their involvement or leave? | [Make Entry and Changes of Participation Workable (CB.3)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb3---make-entry-and-changes-of-participation-workable) | An understandable next action with access to a response or help, and a workable way to reduce or decline involvement. |
| Which space and shared activity fit the purpose? | [Design a Space and Shared Activity for Its Purpose (CB.4)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb4---design-a-space-and-shared-activity-for-its-purpose) | A feasible activity whose result or unresolved question reaches its next use. |
| How can participants provide a contribution that someone can use? | [Obtain and Return Useful Contributions from Participants (CB.5)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb5---obtain-and-return-useful-contributions-from-participants) | An agreed contribution, receiving use or limitation, and a return to the contributor. |
| How should we recognise a contribution? | [Recognise a Contribution and Choose a Meaningful Response (CB.6)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb6---recognise-a-contribution-and-choose-a-meaningful-response) | A truthful response the contributor can accept, with any offered benefit actually obtainable. |
| How can organising work continue beyond one person, or attention be shared during an activity? | [Prepare and Sustain Distributed Organising (CB.7)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb7---prepare-and-sustain-distributed-organising) | A willing, prepared person or temporary participant group with the time, support and mandate for its next contribution; a feasible successor or a reduced promise when continuity matters. |
| How should participation rules work when an incident or disagreement occurs? | [Make Participation Rules Usable and Resolve Incidents (CB.8)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb8---make-participation-rules-usable-and-resolve-incidents) | An applicable expectation, an authorised next action and a reachable correction or review route. |
| Who can provide the work and resources, and on what terms? | [Provide for Community Work and Agree Its Terms (CB.9)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb9---provide-for-community-work-and-agree-its-terms) | An offer deliverable for a stated period, with actual contributions and a response to lost support; reducing or ending the promise may be appropriate. |
| What value did participation or cultural work produce? | [Understand the Value of Participation and Cultural Work (CB.10)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb10---understand-the-value-of-participation-and-cultural-work) | An account of what happened, what the evidence supports, what remains uncertain and what to continue or change. |
| Should the arrangement continue, change hands, split, pause or end? | [Continue, Change, Transfer or End a Community Arrangement (CB.11)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb11---continue-change-transfer-or-end-a-community-arrangement) | An agreed continuation or ending with receiving work, provision and settlement of remaining commitments. |
| How can someone carry out a useful repeated action of participation? | [Support a Useful Repeated Action of Participation (CB.12)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb12---support-a-useful-repeated-action-of-participation) | A feasible arrangement for one wanted action and a way to examine later opportunities, obstacles or a reason to discontinue it. |
| Who may make a shared decision, and how can it be challenged? | [Establish a Workable Mandate for Shared Decisions (CB.13)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb13---establish-a-workable-mandate-for-shared-decisions) | An effective mandate with understood limits and a challenge route, or the unresolved authority or agreement question. |
| How can a recurring practice difficulty lead to reusable help? | [Develop and Maintain a Shared Repertoire of Practice (CB.14)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb14---develop-and-maintain-a-shared-repertoire-of-practice) | A selected repertoire contribution, a willing and equipped provider and an intended receiving use. |
| How can people from different practices contribute to one useful result? | [Connect Practices through a Useful Joint Contribution (CB.15)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb15---connect-practices-through-a-useful-joint-contribution) | An agreed joint question, each side's contribution, permitted material and access, and a worthwhile return. |
| How can a shared position enter someone else's decision? | [Form and Carry a Collective Voice into a Decision (CB.16)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cb16---form-and-carry-a-collective-voice-into-a-decision) | The receiving decision, relevant positions and uncertainties, and who may present each position on whose behalf. |

The [common applications (CB — Applications)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/COMMUNITY-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#applications) connect these methods for professional repairers, a voluntary garden, independent carriers of a practice and a customer community, with the specialist contributions each case needs.


### Engineering.Reference:1.23 - Make corporate decisions and sustain governing contributions

Use corporate governance to establish relevant rights and powers, arrange governing contributions and perform corporate acts. Financial attractiveness, a recommendation and corporate authority answer different questions. The [connected interested-party example (CGOV — CGOV-CONFLICTED-MATTER - Bring an interested-party transaction to a corporate decision)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov-conflicted-matter---bring-an-interested-party-transaction-to-a-corporate-decision) follows advice, disclosure and eligible participation into a decision; start with already sufficient contributions when they are available.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which corporation, proposed act and rules matter here? | [Frame the Corporate Matter and Its Governing Rules (CGOV.1)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov1---frame-the-corporate-matter-and-its-governing-rules) | A bounded corporate matter and the provisions that change its answer. |
| Does an ownership percentage establish votes or control? | [Distinguish Shareholding, Voting Power, and Control (CGOV.2)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov2---distinguish-shareholding-voting-power-and-control) | The relevant holding, economic right, voting entitlement or control relation, with the appropriate calculation. |
| Who can appoint, remove, approve or sign? | [Establish Authority for Corporate Appointments, Removals, and Decisions (CGOV.3)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov3---establish-authority-for-corporate-appointments-removals-and-decisions) | The applicable power and its conditions. A sufficient existing delegation can answer the question. |
| What contribution should the board and executives each provide? | [Design Board and Executive Contributions (CGOV.4)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov4---design-board-and-executive-contributions) | A design for the needed work and its result exchanges under the corporate powers. |
| Do we need a committee, and can its findings be used? | [Choose an Arrangement for Independent Corporate Oversight, with or without a Committee (CGOV.5)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov5---choose-an-arrangement-for-independent-corporate-oversight-with-or-without-a-committee) | A design for a permitted oversight arrangement, with its remit, participants, support and receiving use. |
| Does a director's or owner's interest affect this matter? | [Expose Conflicts and Related-Party Interests (CGOV.6)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov6---expose-conflicts-and-related-party-interests) | The relevant interest, conflict conditions and required safeguards. |
| What independent review or participation arrangement is needed? | [Arrange Independent Review and a Disinterested Corporate Decision (CGOV.7)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov7---arrange-independent-review-and-a-disinterested-corporate-decision) | Usable review findings and an eligible decision arrangement, retaining the separate corporate act. |
| What information is owed, to whom and when? | [Provide Corporate Information under Applicable Rights and Duties (CGOV.8)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov8---provide-corporate-information-under-applicable-rights-and-duties) | Required content provided through usable access, with confidentiality requirements and the limits of specialist conclusions preserved. |
| Will the proposed control actually operate in the work? | [Establish and Operate Internal Control (CGOV.9)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov9---establish-and-operate-internal-control) | A control and the means to operate it, with supported effectiveness and its limits kept distinct. |
| What can this audit or assurance conclusion support? | [Obtain and Use a Scoped Audit or Assurance Conclusion for Corporate Governance (CGOV.10)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov10---obtain-and-use-a-scoped-audit-or-assurance-conclusion-for-corporate-governance) | A contribution qualified by its subject, criteria, period, provider and limitations. |
| Has the corporate decision been made, or only described? | [Make and Record a Corporate Decision (CGOV.11)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov11---make-and-record-a-corporate-decision) | The act performed through the applicable procedure and its proper record, with remaining conditions clear. |
| How can a minority holder protect or exercise a right? | [Protect Corporate Minority Holders' Rights and Enable Contest or Exit (CGOV.12)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov12---protect-corporate-minority-holders-rights-and-enable-contest-or-exit) | A timely use of an available protection, exercise, contest or exit route under its actual conditions. |
| What response should follow a performance exception? | [Monitor Corporate Performance and Require an Account (CGOV.13)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov13---monitor-corporate-performance-and-require-an-account) | An account against the undertaking, an authorized response and follow-up on its consequence. |
| Should a governing instrument or arrangement change, and how? | [Decide Whether and How to Change Corporate Governing Instruments and Arrangements (CGOV.14)](../Management%20DPF%20Suite/CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov14---decide-whether-and-how-to-change-corporate-governing-instruments-and-arrangements) | A supported decision to retain the arrangement or repair its operation, or a revision made effective through the current amendment powers and required acts, with implementation addressed. |
